jobs.occupation: International Clinician Scientist (f/d/m) for iPRACTIS (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
Die Medizinische Hochschule Hannover (MHH), mit rund 10.000 Beschäftigten größter Landesbetrieb des Landes Niedersachsen, ist eine universitäre Einrichtung für Forschung und Lehre in der Human- und Zahnmedizin und ein Universitätsklinikum der Supramaximalversorgung. Forschung, Lehre, Krankenversorgung und Administration arbeiten im Integrationsmodell auf dem MHH-Campus Hand in Hand.
About us

Hannover Medical School (MHH) is offering positions in the international clinician scientist program (iPRACTIS), a unique opportunity for internationally mobile researchers with a completed medical degree outside of Germany. Over three years, you will gain experience in translational research while working towards medical degree recognition in Germany.

iPRACTIS supports internationally trained researchers aiming to build careers in academic medicine. Over three years, participants will deepen their research experience on a translational research project while working towards integration into the German academic and healthcare system.

We offer

The international clinician scientist program iPRACTIS offers:

- 36 months of structured clinical and scientific training based on an individually tailored career plan
- Individualized support in navigating the process of medical degree recognition in Germany and developing German language proficiency
- Funding for materials, travel, and publication
- Individualized support from a personalized mentoring team
- A curriculum to acquire key competencies [including data management and analysis, GCP clinical investigator certification (GCP-Prüfarztkurs), project management]
- Regular evaluations and feedback meetings
- A full onboarding program and integration into a strong Clinician Scientist Network

Clinical expectations: Participants will achieve recognition of their medical qualifications along with sufficient German language skills for clinical practice, allowing future specialist training and medical practice in Germany.

Research expectations: Participants will develop as a R2 researcher (according to the European Framework for Research Careers), including submitting their first third-party funding application. Participants who complete this process will be ready to pursue an independent research career (R3) in roles such as assistant professor, principal investigator, or junior group leader.

Eligibility requirements

To apply, candidates must:

- Hold a completed medical degree (from outside Germany)
- Have initial research experience (completed R1 to early R2 based on European Framework for Research Careers)
- Have not yet completed specialist clinical training (residency or German 'Facharzt' / 'Weiterbildung' equivalent)
- Be committed to pursuing a career combining clinical practice and research

In order to consider your application, we require that you submit the completed "iPRACTIS Application Template" (download) as well as a cover letter and detailed resume (in table format), a declaration of consent and copies of certificates (medical examination certificates, doctoral degree certificates, high school diplomas, and other relevant certificates and documents. If the documents are not in German or English, a certified translation is requested). Please submit your application as a single PDF file directly to practis@mh-hannover.de. More information can be found at iPRACTIS.

External applications for iPRACTIS positions will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The deadline for internal applications is 05.01.2027.
For questions, please reach out to Dr. Thorsten Saenger: practis@mh-hannover.de.

Postdoctoral Researcher CMS Experiment

Remuneration Group 13 | Limited: 5 years | Starting date: earliest possible | ID: FHPO009/2026 | Deadline: 24.09.2026 | Remote work possible

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

The CMS DESY group is based in Hamburg and is one of the largest groups worldwide participating in the CMS Experiment at CERN. The successful candidate will join a newly established Helmholtz Investigator Group at DESY, working within the CMS Collaboration to study how top quarks interact with the heavy bosons (W, Z, and Higgs) at the highest energies reached at the LHC. Using the full CMS dataset, the project targets these interactions in the boosted regime and interprets the measurements in the framework of Effective Field Theory, searching for subtle deviations from the Standard Model that could point to new physics. The work combines advanced jet reconstruction and identification with modern machine-learning techniques, offering the opportunity to develop expertise at the interface of experimental data analysis and cutting-edge ML methods.

About your role:

- Develop and apply advanced jet reconstruction and machine-learning techniques for the identification of boosted top quarks and heavy bosons, forming the methodological foundation shared across the group's measurements.
- Take a leading role in the unfolding of the differential cross-section measurements and in the global Effective Field Theory interpretation combining them into constraints on top-boson couplings.

Postdoctoral researcher

Limited: 2 years | Start: 01.12.2026 | ID: FHPO008/2026 | Deadline: 30.09.2026 | Full-time/Part-time | Remote work possible

DESY, with more than 2900 employees at its two locations in Hamburg and Zeuthen, is one of the world's leading research centres. Its research focuses on decoding the structure and function of matter, from the smallest particles of the universe to the building blocks of life. In this way, DESY contributes to solving the major questions and urgent challenges facing science, society and industry. With its ultramodern research infrastructure, its interdisciplinary research platforms and its international networks, DESY offers a highly attractive working environment in the fields of science, technology and administration as well as for the education of highly qualified young scientists.

The particle physics programme of DESY includes strong contributions to the LHC experiments at CERN and the preparation of future experiments. The experimental programme is enhanced by collaboration with a strong theory group. The DESY ATLAS group is involved in data analyses focusing on W and Z production, Higgs, top quark and Beyond Standard Model physics. In addition the group is involved in the operation of the ATLAS detector and developments for future upgrades, such as the ATLAS silicon strip tracker for the High Luminosity LHC. A new Emmy Noether group within the ATLAS group will be addressing limitations to the measurement of total Higgs boson decay rates by scrutinizing some of the foundational assumptions underlying these measurements and identifying areas where these assumptions can be reevaluated or relaxed. We are Hiring a postdoc to join the new Emmy Noether group and contribute to these measurements.

About your role:

- Higgs boson width determination using H->ZZ events
- Tests of the stability of the measurement with respect to various assumptions, specifically looking into the effect of several free parameters
- Perform EFT fits to constrain potential BSM effects
- Daily supervision of students working on these topics
- Contributing to the performance studies of ATLAS

About you:

- PhD in experimental particle physics
- Experience in the analysis of big data
- Familiar with EFT frameworks (specifically event generation with EFT models)
- Familiar with statistical analysis tools
- Able to handle combinations of different particle physics measurements
- Excellent English skills

Good reasons to join:

Look forward to a unique working environment on our international research campus. Respectful cooperation and the well-being of our DESY employees are particularly important to us. Gender equality is an important aspect for us. To support work life balance we offer flexible working hours, variable part-time, job-sharing models and participation in mobile work (up to 50%). You will benefit from our family-friendly and collegial atmosphere, our established health management and occupational pension provision. As a public funded employer, we offer you a secure workplace and facilitate your individual career with our comprehensive training and development opportunities. Remuneration is according to the regulations of the TV-AVH. DESY offers its employees a financial supplement for a German job ticket (Deutschland-Ticket) at both locations.

For further information please contact Dr. Martina Ojeda at atlas-contact@desy.de

Please submit your complete application documents (letter of motivation and research interests, CV, list of publications, relevant certificates and three letters of references). Please use our online tool for the submission of the letters of reference: Additional application documents (https://www.desy.de/career/additional_application_documents/index_eng.html)

- Develop and execute a multi-year global roadmap for contamination control and sterility assurance across biologics, small molecules, sterile fill-finish, ADCs, and new modalities.

- Expertise in EU GMP Annex 1, ISO 14644, USP, PDA technical reports, and related regulatory frameworks for aseptic/low-bioburden manufacturing.

jobs.description:
In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number of

Postdoctoral Researcher positions.

- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -

The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. 

The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department currently hosts Ramin Golestanian (director), Philip Bittihn (group leader), Suropriya Saha (group leader), and a number of postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.

The research

The postdoctoral researchers will engage in theoretical and computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter. For more information, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).

Your profile

We are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated researchers with relevant background and good communication skills to join our research team. 

The ideal candidate should have:

- A PhD/DPhil degree (or comparable) with a background in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;
- Prior experience with nonequilibrium statistical physics and a strong interest in active matter physics;
- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;
- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.

Our offer

We are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary is in accordance with the German state public service salary scale (E13 TVöD-Bund) and the corresponding social benefits. Working hours are full time. We offer opportunities regarding work life balance as well as health promotion services. The postdoctoral appointment is for two years. The starting date is flexible.

The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. We encourage applications from women, especially in areas where they are underrepresented, which includes theoretical physics. Moreover, we are committed to providing suitable working environment for everyone including individuals with disabilities.

Your application

To apply, please follow this link (https://s.b-ite.com/vd1cg)  and submit your CV, publication list, a statement of research interest, and contacts of two referees. In addition to the description of your proposed research, it should also briefly describe your past and current research interests and why you are interested in joining our department. Processing of applications will start after the deadline of 10th January 2027, and will stop when the positions are filled.

Earlier this year (March 2026), Unilever announced an agreement to separate our Foods business. Our Foods business, including brands such as Hellmann's and Knorr, will join forces with McCormick to become a global flavour leader, with leading positions across spices, seasonings, condiments and complementary food categories, supported by a strong retail and food service platform. McCormick has 135+ years of heritage, a presence in 150+ countries and territories, and a portfolio of trusted brands. The transaction remains subject to consultation, regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions with a targeted deal close of mid-2027.

This role exists to act as a key link between global, regional, and local stakeholders, providing broad cross-functional exposure and fostering collaboration across Unilever and the future separated Foods business.

You’ll be part of a team that believes in doing work that matters — for people and the planet.

Because here, we don’t just hire for jobs. We invite you to be part of something bigger.

- Lead and coordinate a major business transformation initiative in Germany.

Join the Cluster of Excellence "BlueMat: Water-Driven Materials" ( www.tuhh.de/bluemat ) and collaborate with a dynamic, interdisciplinary team that combines science, sustainability, and technology to create a better future. Help shape the next generation of sustainable materials inspired by nature's most powerful resource: water.

For the Institute of Metallic Biomaterials, Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon for as soon as possible, we are looking for a Postdoctoral Researcher - Agentic Correlative Image Analysis for BlueMaterials. In principle, the full time position (39 h/week) is also sharable. The position is fixed-term until 31 August 2029 and located in Rostock.

Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position.

The BlueMat project 'Agentic correlative image analysis for BlueMaterials', bridges the different imaging and characterization techniques developed within the cross-area imaging and gives support to all researchers in the cluster of excellence to retrieve the highest quality information from image data. The project focusses on implementing an agentic framework for automation of correlative imaging and the corresponding image analysis in particular. By implementing LLM-driven agents that plan the analysis workflow, call established image-analysis modules and judge their own output, you will streamline image processing efforts and enable the elucidation of specific mechanisms of water-material interactions.

design and implement the agentic framework including task planning, tool use and function calling, and self-evaluation loops that orchestrate existing image-analysis modules
build a natural-language interface so BlueMat researchers can run correlative analyses without writing code
automate including image registration and enabling automated extraction of morphological features (e.g., porosity, tortuosity, connectivity) and fluid flow characteristics from 2D and 3D images resulting from magnetic resonance, X-ray and electron images
integration of motion analysis and digital volume correlation
processing of images in preparation for image-based modelling
individual support for researchers across BlueMat in solving image analysis challenges, especially segmentation and quantitative extraction

experience in building LLM-based agent systems
strong background in image processing and analysis, including deep learning
experience with correlative imaging workflows and 2D/3D registration techniques
strong programming skills in Python and/or C/C++
ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary environment

Quantum Computing Expert (m/f/d)

to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C), full-time (39 hours perweek), remunerated in accordance with TVöD E 13. The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing centerfor the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society.The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the Universityof Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers (NHR-Nord@Göttingen) in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is apartner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Furthermore, the GWDG operates HPC resources for the GermanAerospace Center (DLR). As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG provides technical support to researchersand students from various scientific domains, including digital humanities, life science, earth system science, andengineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. In the field of quantumcomputing, the GWDG also runs the QUICS project, providing SMEs with access to quantum computing resources.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates to join the QC team at the GWDG focused on anomaly detection forindustry applications. The goal is to build a platform for such use cases based on existing stacks, giving companies atool for quantum anomaly detection.

The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science(CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with anopportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing,Quantum Computing, and AI.

Responsibilities

Focus:

Integration of quantum-based algorithms into classical computing environments, and system-levelstability/error analysis of the integrated hybrid stack.

The role goes beyond merely operating existing quantum software stacks. It also involves designing modular,hardware-agnostic backends capable of seamlessly integrating both simulators and current NISQ devices. Thisrequires:

Running simulations on HPC systems, including efficiently parallelizing computational tasks

Writing HPC-executable, production-ready code

Ensuring scalability and robustness of algorithms in large-scale environments

Identifying and resolving error sources in the integrated hybrid stack, particularly cascading errors acrossmodules

Developing independent code for simulations, extending beyond the use of standard software libraries

Requirements

PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, combined with demonstrableindustry or research experience

Proven coding experience (without AI assistance): scope, functions, variables, classes, array methods, etc.

Good knowledge of diverse quantum hardware, error correction/mitigation strategies, and respective SDKecosystems (Qiskit, Cirq, Braket, Qrisp, AutoQML, etc.)

Advanced linear algebra knowledge: matrix diagonalization methods, magnus expansion, Zassenhausformula, group theory

Advanced quantum physics knowledge: quantum circuit design, Trotterization, quantum machine learning, etc

Demonstrated experience running simulations on HPC systems

Excellent teamwork and communication skills

Fluent English (spoken and written)

Do you fit all the above requirements? Then we welcome your application!

Desirable

Hands-on experience with multiple quantum SDKs (Qiskit, Cirq, Amazon Braket, PennyLane)

Experience implementing or working with quantum error mitigation/correction techniques

Experience running large-scale quantum simulations on HPC clusters (e.g., GPU-accelerated state-vector ortensor-network simulators)

Contributions to open-source quantum computing libraries, or published work on quantum algorithms

Familiarity with ion-trap or other NISQ hardware platforms

Knowledge in writing bash scripts for HPC job submission

German B2 or higher

A modern, diverse work environment at the intersection between academia and industry

An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center

Qualification and further development of your skills

Social benefits of the public sector

jobs.occupation: Research Associate / Postdoc (m/f/d) in the field of Cryogenic Quantum Electronics (Physiker/in)
jobs.description:
With around 15.000 students and 3.800 employees, the Technische Universität Braunschweig is one of Germany’s leading institutes of technology. It stands for strategic and performance-oriented thinking and acting, relevant research, committed teaching, and the successful transfer of knowledge and technologies to the economy and society. We consistently advocate for family friendliness and equal opportunities.

Our research focuses are mobility, engineering for health, metrology, and city of the future. Strong engineering and natural sciences are our core disciplines. These are closely interconnected with economics, social and educational sciences and humanities. Our campus is located in the midst of one of the most research-intensive regions in Europe. We work successfully together with over 20 research institutions in our neighborhood as we do with our international partner universities.

The Division of Cryogenic Quantum Electronics, led by Prof. Dr. Oleksandr Dobrovolskiy, investigates fascinating physical phenomena governing the dynamics of magnetic and superconducting systems and develops quantum electronic devices based on these principles. Its research bridges materials science, experimental physics, electrical measurement science, and metrology. To strengthen the research group and advance its cutting-edge research in cryogenic quantum electronics, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher (m/f/d)
(EG13 TV-L, full time - fixed term)

with demonstrated expertise in experimental low-temperature physics.
The position is to be filled on a fixed-term basis for an initial period of 2 years. The successful applicant will be given the opportunity to pursue a further scientific qualification (habilitation).

Your tasks

- You will carry out research in the area of cryogenic and quantum electronics, with a focus on experiments at mK temperatures.
- You will apply for and work on research projects.
- You will perform measurements in a dilution refrigerator and other cryogenic setups, develop, build and optimize cryogenic measurement platforms.
- You will publish research findings in leading international journals and participate in national and international conferences.
- You will be involved in teaching at the University (preparation and implementation of courses as well as supervision of students’ work).

Your Qualifications

- You hold a completed university degree at Master’s level or equivalent, as well as a completed PhD in a field relevant to the position (e.g. physics, electrical engineering, materials science, or a related field), and ideally have postdoctoral research experience.
- You have experience with low-temperature experiments, ideally involving dilution refrigerators in the fields of superconductivity and/or magnetism, as well as good programming skills (e.g., Python, LabVIEW).
- You have knowledge of superconducting and/or magnetic devices, high-frequency and microwave engineering, nanotechnology, and/or quantum measurement techniques, or you are willing and able to acquire this expertise quickly.
- You have excellent English language skills; knowledge of German is desirable.
- You are flexible, can perform under pressure and work well in a team.

We offer

- work on exciting future-oriented research topics in an inspiring work environment as part of the university community
- A vibrant campus life in an international atmosphere with lots of intercultural offers and international cooperations
- Pay in accordance with the collective agreement TV-L (a special payment at the end of the year as well as a supplementary benefit in the form of a company pension, comparable to a company pension in the private sector) including 30 days' vacation per year
- flexible working and part-time options and a family-friendly university culture, awarded the "Family-friendly university" audit since 2007
- special continuing education programs for young scientists, a postdoc program, as well as other offerings from the Central Personnel Development Department and sports activities.

Further notes
We welcome applicants of all nationalities. At the same time, we encourage people with severe disabilities to apply. Applications from severely disabled persons will be given preference if they are equally qualified. Please attach a proof of disability to your application. We are also working on the fulfilment of the Central Equality Plan based on the Lower Saxony Equal Rights Act (Niedersächsisches Gleichberechtigungsgesetz—NGG) and strive to reduce under-representation in all areas and positions as defined by the NGG. Therefore, applications from women are particularly welcome in this case.

By submitting your application, you agree that your data may be stored and processed electronically for application purposes in compliance with the provisions of data protection law. Further information on data protection can be found in our data protection regulations at https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/datenschutzerklaerung-bewerbungen (https://www.tu-braunschweig.de/datenschutzerklaerung-bewerbungen) .

The Business Process Engineer for Third-Party Risk Management is responsible for designing, optimizing, and continuously improving the end-to-end processes that support the identification, assessment, monitoring, and management of third-party (vendor, supplier, outsourcing) risk across the organization.
The role bridges risk management requirements with operational execution, translating regulatory and policy requirements (e.g., DORA, outsourcing guidelines) into efficient, scalable, and auditable workflows.
This role will be based in Frankfurt.

What you will do

- Process Design & Optimization: Map, analyse, and redesign TPRM lifecycle processes (onboarding, due diligence, risk assessment, contracting, ongoing monitoring, offboarding) to improve efficiency, consistency, and control effectiveness
- Workflow & Tooling: design and implement defined TPRM workflow in the Sourcing & Procurement ServiceNow Platform. Configure, enhance, and maintain workflow tools (e.g. ServiceNow, Databricks) that support process execution and data capture
- Align and harmonize the Procurement and TPRM workflows as an integrated workflow
- Requirements Translation: Work with Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Procurement to translate regulatory obligations (such as DORA ICT third-party risk requirements) and internal policy into operational process steps and control points as part of the workflow
- Documentation & Governance: Create and maintain process maps, standard operating procedures (SOPs), RACI matrices, and control documentation; ensure processes are inventoried and governed per internal EUC/process governance standards
- Reporting: Define and track process KPIs/KRIs (e.g., cycle times, SLA adherence, backlog, exception rates) to support management reporting and continuous improvement
- Stakeholder Engagement: Act as a liaison between TPRM, business units, IT, Procurement, and second-line risk functions to ensure process changes are understood, adopted, and sustainable
- Change Management: Lead process changes initiatives, including impact assessment, testing, training, and rollout of new or revised procedures
- AI and Continuous Improvement: Identify automation opportunities (e.g., Multi AI Agent orchestration, workflow automation, questionnaire logic, risk scoring rules) and work with relevant teams to implement them, subject to governance and review requirements
- Quality & Control: Support internal audit, regulatory exam, and quality assurance activities by ensuring processes are well-documented, consistently applied, and evidenced
- RUN & Governance Responsibility: Ensure the Oversight and RUN activities for the Third-Party Risk Management team

What you bring

- Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Risk Management, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field
- 6+ years of experience in business process engineering, process improvement, or operations roles, ideally within financial services or asset management
- Prior exposure to Third-Party Risk Management, vendor management, outsourcing oversight, or operational risk is highly desirable
- Familiarity with process improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean, Six Sigma, BPMN) and process mapping tools
- Understanding of relevant regulatory frameworks (e.g., DORA, EBA/ESMA outsourcing guidelines) is a plus
- Experience with GRC or TPRM platforms (e.g., ServiceNow, Archer, OneTrust, or similar) or Databricks preferred
- Being a team player
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
- Proactive and client-centric approach, combining diplomacy and assertiveness
- Proficiency in English required, further languages would be highly helpful, German is a plus
- AI Skills such as Microsoft Copilot, Feature Engineering, Data Engineering

We are looking for a gifted student who loves models, algorithms, and data,

problem over the next three years. You should have a recent Master's degree in

area. A Master's thesis on an ML topic and ML-related courses in your Master's

About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

Airbus Defence and Space is looking for

Vertragsjurist / Procurement Contracts Manager (d/m/w)

Airbus Defence and Space is looking for a Procurement Contracts Manager (m/f) to join our "Procurement Contracts department" dedicated to the Space Systems Business line. The successful candidate will be based in Bremen, Germany.

Are you ready to shape the future of aerospace and defense? Join our diverse, international team of 30+ Contract Managers and become a vital part of our Air Power, Space, and Connected Intelligence divisions. Join a dedicated team that acts every day true to the global Airbus purpose: “We pioneer sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world”.

Here, you won't just manage contracts, you will provide the strategic expertise that powers our Procurement function and supports the development of next-generation Space Systems for global commercial and governmental customers. You will work at the intersection of innovation and execution, collaborating closely with experts in Sales, Finance, Legal, and Export Control.

If you are looking for a high-impact role in a supportive, multicultural environment, we want to hear from you.

** Your Location**

Bremen is a charming, historic city in the northwest of Germany. It is not only one of the greenest cities in the country, but also offers wonderful sights, a rich culture, urban flair and culinary delights. The city is also a great place for coastal lovers, as it is only a one-hour drive away from the North Sea coast.

** Our Benefits for you**

- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive salary and individual additional benefits, e.g. company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g. bicycle leasing) or employee advantages at cooperating companies in accordance with our valid guidelines.
- Time for you (and your relatives): 30 days of annual leave according to the collective agreement (35h/week); compatibility of family & career (flextime, mobile working, part-time, job sharing, sabbatical).
- Easy Progression: Excellent further training opportunities and international, group-wide development perspectives.
- Well-being at work: Company doctor; comprehensive health offers (sports courses, prevention offers, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, partly near-site kindergarten.
- Diversity connects: Working in a diverse environment, with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, support and diversity are lived.

** Your Tasks and Responsibilities**

- Act as the Procurement Contract Manager (“PCM”) Focal Point for applicable Space Systems business activities and programs, mainly in Germany,
- Provide the support and drive your advice of Call for Tenders (CFTs) by challenging/assessing/approving the contractual baselines, assessing the contractual elements of bids, preparing/supporting the negotiations and overseeing the contract awards,
- Prepare, perform and lead contract drafting and negotiations in close collaboration with the Procurement function,
- Approve and sign the Contract Validation Form (CVF) ensuring all key elements - including executive summaries, deviations, risks, and opportunities - are accurately captured and approved, prior to any Airbus final signature,
- Hand in hands with the Procurement function, oversee and manage the contract lifecycle, including: preparation, drafting and negotiation of complex contracts, amendments, claims and settlement agreements, and other key contractual documents,
- Mitigate contractual risks by providing contractual expert analysis and advice during disagreements or potential disputes between Airbus and our partners, suppliers,
- Provide support for the preparation/defense of claims and pre-litigation matters,
- Provide cross-functional expertise in contract design, drafting, and negotiation for Airbus departments outside of the Procurement function,
- Advise internal stakeholders on the contractual implications of strategic projects, specifically, but not only, regarding confidentiality and Intellectual Property (IP),
- Develop new and further development of existing Procurement Academy training; coaching and training-on-the-job of our stakeholders in the areas of contracts management and negotiations,
- In the objectives to enhance performance and agility, standardize procurement excellence by proposing, drafting and revising standard contracts that integrate economic, commercial, technological, legal, and risk management requirements.

** Required Skills and Qualifications**

- You hold a successfully completed university degree (Master's level) in Legal and/or Business Administration or equivalent, with experience in Contact Management, Business Law, or a comparable experience.
- You possess a good experience in Contract Management as well as in the legally secure drafting and design of procurement agreements (3+ years).
- You communicate at a fully negotiation-proof level in German and have fluent English language skills to cooperate effectively in an international context. German language is mandatory.
- Your are open-minded, self-motivated team-player, you provide a “Can Do” attitude who enjoys finding solutions to contractual issues / challenges,
- You are Customer oriented, with excellent communication and collaboration skills,
- Analytical and rigorous, able to break-down and explain complex topics to a variety of stakeholders,
- Pragmatic, able to balance contractual and business risks, priorities, oversights and compliance,
- Willing to take on big and small tasks, ranging from operational support to strategic projects.

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal development with tailored development solutions. Take your career to the next level and apply online now!

Job description

In order to support Airframe Engineering, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Fatigue & Damage Tolerance Engineer (d/f/m)

Become part of a pioneering team with a strong identity and a shared commitment to delivering best-in-class stress solutions!

​Join the Fuselage Structure Analysis team in Hamburg as a technical anchor in our newly integrated "One Fuselage" domain. As the Fatigue & Damage Tolerance (F&DT) Engineer for Primary Structure, you will will have the chance of contributing to the structural integrity, driving the F&DT justification for critical fuselage components across the entire aircraft lifecycle—from next-generation design and certification to manufacturing and global fleet support.

You will grow into a technical expert, collaborating with a high-level network to integrate advanced simulations and structural health strategies. We are looking for a motivated, curious engineer driven by a "People First" spirit to help us create the future of aerospace excellence.

This role is also available with reduced weekly hours and an adapted scope of tasks.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and special payments
- 30 days paid vacation and extra days-off for special occasions
- Excellent upskilling opportunities and great international, group wide development prospects
- Special benefits: employer-funded pension, employee stock options, discounted car leasing, special conditions for insurances, transportation subsidy, employee benefits at cooperating companies
- On-site-facilities: Kindergarten close to the site, medical officer for check-ups and other health-related services, canteen and cafeteria
- Compatibility of family & work (job sharing, part-time models, flexible working hours, individual timeout)
- Working in a diverse environment, with more than 140 nationalities, where every voice is heard

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Structural Analysis: Analyze and Validate composite & hybrid structures for Fatigue and Damage Tolerance according to validated methods.
- Airworthiness & Maintenance Criteria: Ensure adherence to relevant regulations, relevant design principles, processes, methods and manufacturing capabilities guidelines.
- Structural Testing: Participate in the planning and analysis of fatigue tests, helping to validate theoretical models with real-world data
- Cross-Functional Certification: Collaborate with Design, Materials, and Stress teams to learn how F&DT requirements are integrated into the earliest design phases
- Support Fleet In-Service Solutions: Provide stress analysis for the repair/acceptance of damaged structures
- Manage Technical Project Deliverables: Define technical scopes, workload sizing, and lead times, ensuring high-quality inputs and the mitigation of technical risks/opportunities
- Continuous Innovation & Method Improvement: Contribute to the evolution of internal analysis tools and structural health monitoring strategies.

​In essence, you will support the delivery of technical outputs in Time, Cost, and Quality, guided by senior experts and technical leadears.

Desired skills and qualifications

- You hold a Master's degree / Diploma in Engineering or similar qualifications
- You bring first experience in Fatigue & Damage Tolerance and associated Process, Methods & Tools
- You enjoy working with many interfaces with different knowledge levels and cultural backgrounds adapting your communication accordingly
- You have a creative data-driven mindset and are motivated to improve the way we work and interact with the world around us (e.g. using AI)
- You have the capabilities to interpret the environmental context and influence decision-making within the company
- Experience in Hyperworks and Python would be a plus
- Fluency in English is mandatory, German is appreciated

Job Description

About the role

As Senior Characterization Engineer (m/f/d), you will join our talented and ambitious R&D team, directly contributing to our ability to successfully produce Gallium Nitride (GaN) devices.

What you will do

- Lead electrical verification strategy, encompassing front-end, back-end and lab testing
- Coordinate the development and implementation of test methodologies for GaN devices, including both wafer-level and product-level testing
- Lead test and characterization concepts and implementation initiatives, and propose new test and characterization setups to solve issues, considering all product aspects from design-to-manufacturing to effective cost structure
- Collaborate closely with device, product, and application engineers to develop test solutions that benefit product development, quality, and customer requirements
- Own test and characterization concepts and implementation. Solve issues and propose new solutions for test and characterization setups

What you will need

- Masters or Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering or Solid-State Physics
- Minimum 3 years of relevant work experience depending on educational credentials
- Specific know-how and hands-on experience in semiconductor characterization methods, especially for GaN technology
- Experience in the test and characterization of high voltage power semiconductor devices, familiarity with Automatic Test Equipment (ATE) desirable but not required
- Team player with strong problem-solving skills and a continuous improvement mindset
- Good communication skills in English (both spoken and written), German a plus

About the role

The Master Data / PLM Specialist is responsible for maintaining accurate product master data, Bills of Material (BOMs), and SAP production data throughout the product lifecycle. This role supports product releases, engineering changes, and new product introductions while ensuring data quality, governance compliance, and effective cross-functional collaboration across Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and Quality teams.

Please note that this is a 12 month temporary assignment.

This is your new role:

- Product Data & BOM Maintenance: Create, update, and maintain product data and Bills of Material (BOMs), ensuring accuracy, consistency, and correct versioning throughout the product lifecycle.
- Change & Release Support: Support New Product Introductions (NPI) and updates by coordinating release readiness, verifying completeness, performing impact analysis, and assisting with approvals and release activities in PLM or related systems.
- SAP Production Material Master: Create and maintain SAP Production Material Masters and Production Versions to support production planning and execution.
- Data Quality & Governance: Apply data standards, naming conventions, and governance rules to maintain high data quality and prevent issues that could impact internal processes or customer-facing systems.
- Cross-functional Coordination: Collaborate closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Quality, and other teams to ensure timely data updates, smooth approvals, and clear communication across stakeholders.
- Process Improvement & System Adoption: Support continuous improvement initiatives by documenting and optimizing workflows, promoting best practices, delivering training, and driving adoption of PLM systems across teams.

This is you:

- Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, IT or a related field or similar education with multiple years experience on a related field.
- Minimum 2 years of experience in data management, product administration, engineering support, or operational coordination, depending on educational credentials.
- Experience with PLM, ERP, or supply chain systems (Enovia, SAP, o9, or similar) is an advantage.
- Basic understanding of master data management, data accuracy, and structured processes.
- Hands-on working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and basic data analysis.
- Strong attention to detail and a structured, organized way of working.
- Good verbal and written communication skills in English (German will be an advantage)
- Collaborative mindset, with experience working in cross-functional teams.
- Proactive, supportive attitude with motivation to learn and grow in the role

HR & Administration Manager

Key Responsibilities

- Oversee daily office operations, including reception duties, mail handling, and supply management.
- Coordinate and organize meetings, appointments, travel arrangements, and company events.

- Support HR with onboarding of new employees (e.g., preparing workstations, access cards etc.).

About us

In order to support the Industrial Architecture Team, Airbus Operations is looking for a

Working student (d/f/m) for Industrial Architecture

You are a full time student, looking for a working student position and want to get to know the work of an Industrial Architect?  Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in department designation as a working student (d/f/m) with approx. 18 hours a week!

At Airbus, Industrial Architecture is driving the next evolution of flight. We are looking for a collaborative, forward-thinking student to join us in shaping the industrial system for our next-generation single-aisle aircraft. If you are passionate about innovation, teamwork, and making a real-world impact, we would love to welcome you to our team.

- Location: Hamburg
- Start: 01.11.2026
- Duration:  12 months

You will receive a collectively agreed salary of at least €18.53 per hour, depending on the job. There are also special payments such as vacation pay.

Definition working student

Working students are students who are enrolled at a University or some other institution of higher education, and who are employed in a reasonably long, fixed-term position parallel to their studies. This position must not be confused with an internship or with the possibility of writing a final thesis.

This employment usually takes place directly on the company's premises. A working student's main focus remains on their studies, which is why, during term-time, working students are not allowed to work more than 20 hours per week.

Working students therefore usually work near their place of study, so as to conveniently combine studying and employment.

Your location: Hamburg Finkenwerder

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Are you wondering how you actually get from university to Airbus? Your working student position is at the Finkenwerder plant and you can take the ferry from Teufelsbrück to the Airbus ferry terminal and back to the university in the morning and at noon. Alternatively, you can take the ferry to Finkenwerder and then ride your bike for about another 15 minutes to the main entrance.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and work-life balance with an 18-hour week (flexitime).
- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.

- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.

Take your career to a new level and apply online (https://www.airbus.com/en/careers) now!

jobs.description:
Job posting no. 20260820

The GWDG is seeking an

HPC Systems & Scheduling Developer (m/f/d)

to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C), full-time (39 hours per week), remunerated in accordance with TVöD E 13. The position is tied to the GWDG QC project’s runtime running till October 2029. The successful candidate is expected to contribute in developing GWDG’s QC ecosystem (see responsibilities listed below). The GWDG handles sensitive data, and in such cases, it is important that the code is human-verified for any security concerns. The applicant must demonstrate the ability to do such a verification without AI assistance in the interview.

The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers (NHR-Nord@Göttingen) in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is a partner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Furthermore, the GWDG operates HPC resources for the German Aerospace Center (DLR). As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG provides technical support to researchers and students from various scientific domains, including digital humanities, life science, earth system science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. In the field of quantum computing, the GWDG also runs the QUICS project, providing SMEs with access to quantum computing resources.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates to join the QC team at the GWDG focused on anomaly detection for industry applications. The goal is to build a platform for such use cases based on existing stacks, giving companies a tool for quantum anomaly detection.

The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, Quantum Computing, and AI.

Responsibilities

Focus: Connecting quantum workloads to GWDG’s existing HPC infrastructure. Requires a deep understanding of both classical HPC architectures and the specific characteristics of quantum jobs. The developer will take responsibility for scheduler logic, including:

- SLURM partition mapping
- Optimization of SLURM execution for Quantum Computing Jobs
- Implement HPC transpilation pipelines and, more generally, workflows for HPC/AI pre- and post-processing
- Performance tuning of hybrid workloads
- Implementation of monitoring and benchmarking mechanisms

Requirements

- PhD and/or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Physics, or a related field, combined with demonstrable industry or research experience
- Ability to code in Python
- Proven coding experience (without AI assistance): scope, functions, variables, classes, array methods, etc.
- Demonstrable expertise in optimizing HPC stacks for proper system implementation and tuning
- Experience building and operating software-based services, ensuring long-term maintainability
- Knowledge in QC (quantum computing) job characteristics and resource requirements, and familiarity with compiler/transpiler pipelines
- Excellent teamwork and communication skills
- Fluent English (spoken and written)

Do you fit all the above requirements? Then we welcome your application!

Desirable

- Demonstrable experience tuning SLURM (partitioning, QoS, job prioritization policies) in a production HPC environment
- Experience benchmarking and profiling hybrid classical/quantum or GPU workloads
- Experience enabling optimal, resource-efficient operation of hybrid classical/quantum workloads
- Familiarity with monitoring and observability tooling for HPC systems (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana)
- Background in systems administration or DevOps for research computing infrastructure
- German B2 or higher

Our offer

- Flexible working hours and opportunity for partial mobile working
- A modern, diverse work environment at the intersection between academia and industry
- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center
- Qualification and further development of your skills
- Social benefits of the public sector

Your application

Have we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 30.09.2026 via our online form: https://bewerbermanagement.net/fpnhs

The GWDG strives for gender equity and diversity and therefore welcomes applications from any background. The GWDG strives to employ more severely disabled people. Applications from severely disabled persons are expressly encouraged.

If you have any questions about the advertised position, please contact Dr. Jan Cillié Louw (e-mail: jancillie.louw@gwdg.de).

The GWDG is seeking a

Quantum Software Engineer (m/f/d)

to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C), full-time (39 hours per week), remunerated in accordance with TVöD E 13. The position is tied to the GWDG QC project’s runtime running till October 2029. The successful candidate is expected to contribute in developing GWDG’s QC ecosystem (see responsibilities listed below). The GWDG handles sensitive data, and in such cases, it is important that the code is human-verified for any security concerns. The applicant must demonstrate the ability to do such a verification without AI assistance in the interview.

The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers (NHR-Nord@Göttingen) in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG also operates the national AI service center KISSKI and is a partner in the EU AI Factory HammerHAI. Furthermore, the GWDG operates HPC resources for the German Aerospace Center (DLR). As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG provides technical support to researchers and students from various scientific domains, including digital humanities, life science, earth system science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. In the field of quantum computing, the GWDG also runs the QUICS project, providing SMEs with access to quantum computing resources.

We are looking for highly motivated candidates to join the QC team at the GWDG focused on anomaly detection for industry applications. The goal is to build a platform for such use cases based on existing stacks, giving companies a tool for quantum anomaly detection.

The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, Quantum Computing, and AI.

Focus: Implementing a containerized FullStaQD instance as a reference implementation for the entire project landscape. This requires a high level of competence in software architecture and quality management. The developer must:

- Implement a modular, scalable infrastructure
- Establish CI/CD pipelines and automated testing frameworks

- Adhere to data protection and security standards (DSGVO-compliant encryption)

- Knowledge of encryption and data protection standards
- Excellent teamwork and communication skills

jobs.occupation: Structural Analysis Engineer VTP (d/f/m) (Ingenieur/in - Luft- und Raumfahrttechnik)
jobs.description:
About us

Airbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. Airbus is also a European leader in defence and security and one of the world's leading space businesses. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.
Job description

In order to support our engineering activities, Airbus Aerostructures is looking for a

Structural Analysis Engineer VTP (d/f/m)

You will be part of a young team of development engineers taking care of the technical steering of projects in the Vertical Tail Plane (VTP) primary and secondary structure perimeter, for the new and incremental development of the complete Single Aisle, WideBody Family and A400M. Working on feasibility studies, supporting the detailed design and in the certification phase, managing structure-driven projects will be part of your job.

Your Location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Our Benefits for You

- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.
- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.
- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.
- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.
- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

Your Tasks and Responsibilities

- Rely on your experience in the domain Fatigue and Damage Tolerance and/or Structure Analysis in order to take over the technical management of related projects
- Analyze and validate composite & hybrid structures for static & fatigue strength according to validated methods and perform related feasibility studies
- Prepare, Check and Approve stress deliverables in line with Airbus’s processes, methods and policies
- Check adherence to airworthiness regulations, relevant design principles, processes, methods and manufacturing capabilities guidelines
- Compile all required documents related to support A/C and MODs certification
- Act as interface for the relevant stakeholders
- Ensure that relevant inputs are provided and fulfill to airworthiness regulations, the Design for the creation of drawings for manufacture and provide support to other functions (i.e. R&T, customer support) as needed
- Perform monitoring and support of Sub-contracting firms providing structure analysis work
- Work on Digitalization, automate and simplify, redesign processes and procedures

****

Desired Skills and Qualifications

- You have a Master Degree (or equivalent) in Engineering, Aerospace, Civil Engineering or comparable
- You have experience in (preferred) Fatigue and Damage Tolerance and/or Structural Analysis methods. This includes experience in finite element method
- You are experienced in tools like ISAMI, FEM e.g. Altair Hyperworks, Nastran, PASS SSCI and TREND
- You hold a technical approval delegation according to Airbus M1020 (for static and/or fatigue) or sufficient experience to obtain this delegation quickly
- You are interested or have an affinity to Data analytics
- You have an open and curious mindset for new ways of working as well as a practical, agile and independent approach
- Your are team-oriented and eager to join a young team in a young organization and shape ways of working
- You are fluent in English and German

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

By submitting your CV or application you are consenting to Airbus using and storing information about you for monitoring purposes relating to your application or future employment. This information will only be used by Airbus.
Airbus is committed to achieving workforce diversity and creating an inclusive working environment. We welcome all applications irrespective of social and cultural background, age, gender, disability, sexual orientation or religious belief.

At Airbus, we support you to work, connect and collaborate more easily and flexibly. Wherever possible, we foster flexible working arrangements to stimulate innovative thinking.

The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 84 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.

The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD). is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.

The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).

The Department for Nanoscale Quantum Materials

is seeking a

Technician (m/f/d) for Laboratory Infrastructure

Your position

We are looking for a hands-on, versatile technician who keeps our laboratories running. You will be the go-to person for the technical infrastructure and day-to-day operations of our experiments. This role complements our engineering and scientific staff, with a focus on practical work, maintenance, and operational readiness.  Your tasks will include:

· **Infrastructure Maintenance:** Independent maintenance, servicing, and monitoring of the laboratory’s technical systems (including vacuum pumps and vacuum systems, gas supply installations, and cryogenic equipment). Implementation of, and adherence to, associated laboratory safety protocols and standards

· **Installations:** Installation and modification of laboratory infrastructure, such as connecting and exchanging pressurized gas cylinders, and routing gas, cooling water, and vacuum lines.

· **Mechanical Assembly:** Planning and executing mechanical work, including the assembly, installation, and relocation of scientific equipment, as well as constructing experimental support frames and enclosures (e.g., using aluminum extrusion profiles). Performing electromechanical tasks such as soldering, crimping, and custom cable/connector assembly.

· **Coordination:** Coordinating deliveries, storage, and workshop logistics; liaising with external service technicians, facility management, and contractors.

· **General Lab Support:** Providing proactive, hands-on assistance for daily laboratory operations as an integral part of the research team.

Your qualification

· **Education:** Completed vocational training (Berufsausbildung) in a relevant technical trade, such as Electronics Technician (Elektroniker/in), Mechatronics Technician (Mechatroniker/in), Precision Mechanic (Feinmechaniker/in), Plant/HVAC Mechanic (Anlagenmechaniker/in), Refrigeration Technician (Mechatroniker/in für Kältetechnik), Physics Laboratory Assistant (Physiklaborant/in), or equivalent skills acquired through substantial professional experience.

· **Work Style:** A strong hands-on mentality, practical problem-solving skills, and genuine enjoyment of a broad, varied range of technical tasks within an active experimental environment. A careful, safety-conscious, and independent approach to work.

· **Language Skills:** A solid command of German (essential for liaising with external contractors and local technical infrastructure) combined with functional, conversational English to communicate within our international research team (or a strong willingness to improve existing English skills).

· **Teamwork:** Team spirit and the flexibility to thrive in a dynamic, evolving research environment.

Desirable, but not required:

· Practical experience with vacuum technology, cryogenics, or the handling of pressurized and liquefied gases.

· Knowledge of low-voltage electrical installations, measurement electronics, or sensor cabling.

Our offer

We offer an innovative environment, which will give you the opportunity to develop your own ideas at the forefront of ultrafast science embedded in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL). We offer a position according to the German public pay scale (TVöD). The position is initially limited to two years, with possibility of extended employment. Collaborations with experimental groups in Hamburg and other locations are planned.

The Max Planck Society and our group specifically strive for gender and diversity equality. We encourage applications from all backgrounds and we are committed to improve gender balance. Furthermore, the Max Planck Society is committed to increasing the number of individuals with disabilities in its workforce and therefore encourages applications from such qualified individuals.

Applications should include a letter of motivation and a curriculum vitae. Please submit your application in English only. The call for this position will close on 13.09.2026.

jobs.description:

Airbus ist Pionier einer nachhaltigen Luft- und Raumfahrt für eine sichere und vereinte Welt. Das Unternehmen arbeitet ständig an Innovationen für effiziente und technologisch fortschrittliche Lösungen in den Bereichen Luft- und Raumfahrt, Verteidigung sowie vernetzte Dienstleistungen. Airbus bietet moderne und treibstoffeffiziente Verkehrsflugzeuge sowie dazugehörige Dienstleistungen an. Airbus ist auch führend in Europa im Bereich Verteidigung und Sicherheit und eines der größten Raumfahrtunternehmen der Welt. Im Bereich Hubschrauber stellt Airbus die weltweit effizientesten Lösungen und Dienstleistungen für zivile und militärische Hubschrauber bereit.
Job description

In order to support our engineering activities, Airbus Aerostructures is looking for a

F&DT Structural Analysis Engineer (d/f/m)

In this role, you will contribute to the structural integrity and safety of Airbus aircraft. As a key member of our Structural Analysis Community, you will handle calculations and support our digital transformation initiatives, collaborating closely with design, production and subcontracting partners.

This role is also available with reduced weekly hours and an adapted scope of tasks.

Your Location

You will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Our Benefits for You

- Fair Compensation & Extras: Attractive remuneration and individual additional benefits, such as company pension schemes, mobility offers (e.g., bike leasing), or corporate discounts with partner companies in accordance with our current guidelines.
- Time for You (and Your Loved Ones): 30 days of annual leave based on our collective agreement (35-hour week); work-life balance through flexible working hours (flextime), mobile working, part-time options, job sharing, and sabbatical opportunities.
- Growth Made Easy: Excellent professional development opportunities and international, group-wide career perspectives.
- Feel Good at Work: On-site company doctor; comprehensive health programs (sports courses, preventive care, etc.), canteen and cafeteria, and local childcare facilities at selected locations.
- Diversity Connects: Work in a diverse environment with more than 140 nationalities, where exchange, mutual support, and inclusion are part of our DNA.

Your Tasks and Responsibilities

- Create analysis models, static and/or F&DT calculations, reports and studies for Airbus aircraft structures (A350XWB and A320 Family)
- Prepare the definition of analysis methods and specifications
- Check internally and externally created analysis data and documentation
- Check relevant input to design for the creation of drawings for manufacturing and support other functions (i.e.: production, customer support) as needed
- Technically guide the sub-contracting companies providing structure analysis work
- Apply airworthiness regulations and relevant design principles
- Define and interpret structural tests for certification
- Monitor project performance
- Support the digital transformation within the structural analysis department by implementing automation, simplifying tools, and redesigning processes.

Desired Skills and Qualifications

- University degree in the engineering / aerospace field or similar qualification acquired in another way
- Experience in the development of aircraft structures (metal & composite) would be a plus
- Knowledge in numerical calculations
- Proficiency in analytical calculation methods (e.g.ISAMI, HSB, Niu, Bruhn)
- Solid knowledge in programming languages (e.g.: Python) and data analytics
- Motivation to work autonomously, take responsibilities and foster communication with all stakeholders
- Open and curious mindset proactively searching for continuous self-development
- English fluency in written and spoken form

Not a 100% match? No worries! Airbus supports your personal growth with customized development solutions.

This job requires an awareness of any potential compliance risks and a commitment to act with integrity, as the foundation for the Company’s success, reputation and sustainable growth

In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number of

PhD positions.

The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. 

The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department is headed by Ramin Golestanian and hosts a number of group leaders, postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.

The research

The PhD students will engage in theoretical and/or computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter, under the supervision of Ramin Golestanian. Your profile

We are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated early-career researchers with good communication skills to join our research team. 

The PhD candidate should have:

- A Master’s degree (or comparable) in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;
- Strong interest in nonequilibrium statistical physics and the physics of living systems across scales;
- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;
- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.

Our offer

We are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary and working hours are in accordance with the funding guidelines of the Max Planck Society for junior scientists. Working hours are fulltime; salary is 2/3 of E13 TVöD-Bund. The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. Become part of a pioneering team with a strong identity and a shared commitment to delivering best-in-class stress solutions!

Join the Fuselage Structure Analysis team in Hamburg as a technical anchor in our newly integrated "One Fuselage" domain. As the Lead Engineer Fatigue & Damage Tolerance (F&DT) for Primary Structure, you will be a custodian of structural integrity, driving the F&DT justification for critical fuselage components across the entire aircraft lifecycle—from next-generation design and certification to manufacturing and global fleet support.

You will lead the delivery of mission-critical stress engineering data and shape the departmental strategy for innovation. This is a pivotal role where you will collaborate across a high-level network to integrate advanced simulations and structural health strategies. We are looking for a pioneering engineer driven by a "People First" spirit to help us create the future of aerospace structural excellence.

This role is also available with reduced weekly hours and an adapted scope of tasks.

Your location - 2 options

Hamburg is home to the largest production site for civil aircraft. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.

Bremen is one of the country’s greenest cities. It offers wonderful sights, a rich culture, urban flair and culinary delights.

Your benefits

- Attractive salary and special payments
- 30 days paid vacation and extra days-off for special occasions
- Excellent upskilling opportunities and great international, group wide development prospects
- Special benefits: employer-funded pension, employee stock options, discounted car leasing, special conditions for insurances, transportation subsidy, employee benefits at cooperating companies
- On-site-facilities: Kindergarten close to the site, medical officer for check-ups and other health-related services, canteen and cafeteria
- Compatibility of family & work (job sharing, part-time models, flexible working hours, individual timeout)
- Working in a diverse environment, with more than 140 nationalities, where every voice is heard

Your tasks and responsibilities

- Lead Advanced Structural Analysis: Technically lead the project team for the fatigue and damage tolerance evaluations
- Define Airworthiness & Maintenance Criteria: Establish damage tolerance philosophies, including allowable damage limits, inspection thresholds, and repeat intervals to ensure long-term structural integrity
- Oversee Structural Testing: Plan and analyze fatigue tests across all levels, validating theoretical models with real-world data
- Drive Cross-Functional Certification: Collaborate with Design, Materials, and Stress teams to integrate F&DT requirements into the design phase, ensuring full compliance with regulatory airworthiness standards
- Support Fleet In-Service Solutions: Investigate structural failures and anomalies to determine root causes, while developing and validating effective repair schemes and service bulletins
- Manage Technical Project Deliverables: Define technical scopes, workload sizing, and lead times, ensuring high-quality inputs and the mitigation of technical risks/opportunities
- Strategic Reporting & Governance: Present progress and technical findings in steering ceremonies, providing clear clarification of assumptions and interdependencies to stakeholders
- Continuous Innovation & Method Improvement: Stay at the forefront of industry advancements to improve internal analysis tools, structural health monitoring strategies, and airworthiness limitation frameworks

In essence, you plan, structure, and deliver technical outputs for your area in Time, Cost and Quality. You guide colleagues and provide technical expertise, supported by senior team members.

Desired skills and qualifications

- You hold a Master's degree / Diploma in Engineering or similar qualifications
- You bring several years of experience in Fatigue & Damage Tolerance and associated Process, Methods & Tools
- You are experienced in technically leading employees
- You enjoy working with many interfaces with different knowledge levels and cultural backgrounds adapting your communication accordingly
- You have a creative data-driven mindset and are motivated to improve the way we work and interact with the world around us (e.g. using AI)
