Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon

The Helmholtz-Zentrum Hereon conducts cutting-edge international research for a changing world: Around 1,000 employees contribute to the tackling of climate change, the sustainable use of the world's coastal systems and the resource-compatible enhancement of the quality of life. From fundamental research to practical applications, the interdisciplinary research spectrum covers a unique range.

Institute of Material Systems Modeling

The Institute of Material Systems Modeling works on methods for virtual material and process development. Computational methods and artificial intelligence are used to optimize materials and their application from the atomic level to the system level.

PhD position in Agentic AI in Computational Modeling

JobID: 1061 - 2026/MS 7
Location: Geesthacht
Application deadline: 23 September, 2026

Developing computational models and running computer simulations in science and engineering still requires substantial expert knowledge. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) offers a great opportunity to automate these demanding tasks to a large extent. We are offering a 3-year position, as soon as possible, as a doctoral student in the area of agentic AI in computational modeling.

Equal opportunity is an important part of our personnel policy. We would therefore strongly encourage qualified women to apply for the position. The position is part-time (planned with 19.5 h/week).
Together with our team, you will push the frontier of agentic AI systems in computational modeling. That is, you will develop systems that leverage agentic AI to automate the development and execution of computer simulations. The objective is creating largely autonomous systems for computational modeling. The main application areas are the various areas of computational science and engineering with a strong focus on computational material science (both at the macroscale and atomic scale), biomedical engineering/biomechanics, and process engineering. However, also applications in environmental modeling (in particular coastal research and climate research) are potentially of interest.
You should have a master's degree in computational engineering, applied mathematics, computer science, or any other field closely related to computational modeling in science and engineering. You have a strong background in the theoretical foundations of engineering, science and applied mathematics. It is an advantage (though not mandatory) if you have prior knowledge in ontologies, knowledge graphs, and/or robotics.

You have demonstrated your excellent skills by outstanding grades during your bachelor's and master's program, in particular in those courses related to this call. You have very good programming skills in Python and ideally also C++. Proven experience in code development is crucial and will be checked during the job interview. Moreover, you have strong skills in communicating science in English.

Introduction

The INM-Leibniz Institute for New Materials is an internationally leading center for interdisciplinary research on materials, and their exploitation in materials-based solutions for a sustainable world with increasing digitalization and medical needs. Our research integrates materials chemistry, biological engineering, physical analysis, process engineering and data science. We collaborate with academic and industrial partners all around the world.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials from the combination of inert materials and living organism, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. Across the institute, materials scientists, synthetic biologists and biophysicists cooperate to understand living and inert matter, and to realize new materials with unprecedented functions from a synergistic interfacing.

We are strongly linked to collaborative initiatives in the ELM field including the Leibniz ScienceCampus LifeMat, Living Therapeutic Materials, the Priority Program SPP2451 “Living Materials with Adaptive Functions”, and the MaterialVital Hub.

As part of our ELM research community, we are seeking a

Postdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Microbial Biophysics (f/m/d)

with interest in the fundamental understanding of microbial communities within synthetic microenvironments. The candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary research team within the Department Dynamic Biomaterials at INM.

Experimental research to understand microbial behaviour in confined spaces (synthetic hydrogels) and dynamic environments using imaging, microfluidics and molecular biology methods.
Scientific cooperation with researchers in materials science and synthetic biology at INM, and with external partners in bioanalytics/bioinformatics within running funded projects.
Compilation and presentation of research results in the form of progress reports and presentations at project meetings and scientific conferences.
Communication of research results within the scientific community at conferences and scientific events, and publication in scientific journals.
Co-supervision of students and doctoral researchers.
Support and promote the digitalization of ELM research in collaboration with dedicated experts in the group.

PhD degree in biophysics/cell biology or related discipline.
Experience during your PhD or previous postdoctoral stay as experimental researcher in the field of microbial biophysics.
Interest in collaborative and interdisciplinary research challenges.
Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.
Very good communication skills in English.

Work in an emergent research topic, with multiple opportunities to develop a competitive research profile.
An interdisciplinary research environment with complementary expertise and ready to share knowledge and support your work.
State-of-the-art infrastructure, including access to Core Facilities run by experts.
Access to a broad international network with vibrant scientific collaborators and exciting cooperation projects.
A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.
A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.
Transparent opportunities for career development.
Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.
A family-friendly working place.
A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.

The position is initially for 2 years.

jobs.occupation: W3 Professorship Computational Social Science (m/f/x; Reference no.: W2906) (Sozialwissenschaftler/in)
jobs.description:
Saarland University is a campus university with a strong international focus and a distinctive research profile characterized by its four core research hubs ‘Computer Science and Informatics’, ‘BioMed’, ‘Europe’ and ‘Sustainability’. With numerous internationally respected research institutes situated in the vicinity of the university and dedicated support for start-up companies, Saarland University is an ideal environment for research, teaching and innovation. The proportion of international students studying at Saarland University is well above the national average and is testimony to the university’s strong international focus. Saarland University has been officially certified as a family-friendly university since 2004.

The Faculty of Human and Business Sciences at Saarland University is inviting applications for the following position to commence in June 2027:

W3 Professorship Computational Social Science (m/f/x; Reference no.: W2906)

The university is also inviting applications for another W2 Professorship (W3 tenure track position) in Political, Social or communication Science (m/f/x; Reference no.: W2905).

This professorial appointment is open regarding the candidate's specific research focus within the field of computational social science. The successful candidate will define their own research agenda, provided that it demonstrates excellence in computational social science, addresses current societal questions, makes use of novel digital data sources and establishes clear links with computer science.

SOUNDS is a research project at Saarland University funded through the Saarland state government’s Transformation Fund. It investigates societally relevant questions through novel digital data sources, digital behavioural traces, social media data and AI-based

methods. This professorship provides the computational social science core of the SOUNDS project. It will combine social-science theory with network analysis, automated text analysis, the study of large-scale digital behavioural data, mobile sensing and AI-based modelling, addressing questions such as collective opinion formation, social cohesion and polarisation, or the role of digital platforms in public communication, and contributing to joint questions, methods and publications with the social sciences and computer science. The successful candidate will be expected to develop and lead externally funded research, including principal investigator roles in coordinated funding initiatives such as Collaborative Research Centres. Teaching duties will include computational and methodological courses, for example on the analysis of digital behavioural data, automated text analysis and network analysis.

These courses will contribute to degree programmes in the social sciences, computer science, data science and psychology. The role also includes the supervision of student theses and the mentoring of early-career researchers. The appointment will be made in accordance with the general provisions of German public sector employment law (see legal recruitment requirements in § 41 Saarländisches Hochschulgesetz, current version available at https://recht.saarland.de/bssl/document/jlr-HSchulGSLrahmen).

We are looking for a researcher with excellent international standing in computational social science and a strong record of working with novel digital data sources applied to societally relevant questions. Your expertise should include computational methods such as network analysis, automated text analysis, the analysis of large-scale digital behavioural data and AIbased modelling. You should be open to a formal affiliation with the Department of Computer Science. You will have an established international research network, an excellent record of high-impact publication and of third-party funding, including grants secured and applications submitted. You should also be prepared to take on principal investigator roles in coordinated funding initiatives such as Collaborative Research Centres. A willingness to teach in English is expected, as is the willingness to teach in German in the medium term.

Saarland University views internationalization as a process spanning all aspects of university life. We therefore expect members of our professorial staff to promote and foster further internationalization. Special support will be provided for projects that expand collaboration within existing international cooperative networks, e.g. projects with partners in the European University Alliance Transform4Europe (www.transform4europe.eu) or the University of the Greater Region (www.uni-gr.eu).

In accordance with the objectives of its gender equality plan, Saarland University is actively seeking to increase the proportion of women in this field. Qualified women candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to apply. Preferential consideration will be given to

applications from disabled candidates of equal eligibility. Furthermore, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates irrespective of nationality, ethnic heritage or social background, religious beliefs, personal beliefs or values, age, sexual orientation or identity.

Please complete the application form in Saarland University's online application portal at www.uni-saarland.de/berufungen and submit it with your application documents by no later than 15 October 2026. Application documents must be uploaded as a single PDF file (max. size 10 MB) and should include the following documents in the order specified:

- Cover letter (addressed to the Dean of the Faculty of Empirical Human Sciences and Economics),
- your résumé detailing your academic career,
- a list of your publications,
- a summary of your research activities and external funding secured to date,
- a list of courses you have taught, sample course evaluations, other evidence of your teaching qualifications,
- a two-page research plan and
- a two-page teaching plan, as well as
- your five most important publications
- Please also include proof of disability if you declared a disability in your application and,
- if you hold a university degree from a foreign university, please provide proof of equivalence from Germany's Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB) if available. If you have not yet requested proof of equivalence from ZAB, you must submit proof at a later

date if so requested. When you submit a job application to Saarland University, you will be transmitting personal data. Please refer to our privacy notice for information on how we collect and process personal data in accordance with Art. 13 of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) (www.uni-saarland.de/en/privacy). By submitting your application, you confirm that you have taken note of the information in the Saarland University privacy notice.

jobs.description:
With about 15,000 students, more than 300 professorships and around 160 degree programs, the RPTU University Kaiserslautern-Landau is the technical university of the state of Rhineland-Palatinate. As a place of top international research, it offers excellent working conditions and career opportunities. Those who study, research or work at RPTU experience a cosmopolitan environment and shape the future.

The position will be part of young research group with a focus on hydrologic process analysis and hydrologic extremes. We use large sample datasets, spatially extensive models and comprehensive literature extraction to gain knowledge on hydrologic behaviour across different spatio-temporal scales. The position is part of the Carl-Zeiss project “AI4ChemRisk” (AI for Chemical Risk Prediction in Aquatic Environments) collaborating with leading research groups in AI, Machine-Learning and Environmental Data Science at the RPTU and abroad.

Your area of responsibility:

- extraction of hydrologic process knowledge from the scientific literature using large language models and natural language processing
- work with sample hydrological data to combine hydrologic process knowledge with chemical risk data
- prediction of hydrological risk factors for aquatic chemical risk
- stakeholder engagement, outreach and collaboration

Your requirements profile:

Applicants should hold an excellent bachelor’s and master’s degree (or equivalent) in hydrology, water resources, or any closely‑related environmental science or in computer science, data science, statistics, or applied mathematics provided they have a demonstrated interest in hydrological processes. Candidates from other quantitative or earth‑system disciplines (e.g., geography, atmospheric science, ecology, civil‑environmental engineering, remote sensing, GIS, environmental physics) are also encouraged to apply if they can show relevant coursework or research experience.

We are looking for a motivated and curious researcher who has

- strong programming proficiency (Python, R, MATLAB, or similar). Experiences with NLP, LLM or high‑performance computing is a plus.
- enthusiasm for interdisciplinary research and collaboration within an international team
- excellent analytical and problem-solving skills
- strong communication skills in English, both written and spoken
- motivation to publish high-quality scientific research and complete a PhD within three years
- work in a motivated, innovative team focusing on data-driven hydrology
- close supervision and individualized mentoring to support your scientific and professional development
- integration into various hydrological research tasks of national to global scopes
- an inspiring, collaborative, and international research environment with strong interdisciplinary interactions
- integration into established national and international research networks and opportunities to present your work at leading scientific conferences
- flexible work environment

RPTU stands for diversity among all employees. We welcome applications from all interested parties, regardless of their ethnic and social origin, age, religion, gender, disability and sexual orientation or identity. Preference will be given to severely disabled persons and persons equivalent to them if they have the appropriate qualifications and suitability.

The RPTU aims to increase the proportion of women in areas where women are underrepresented. Applications from researchers from abroad are expressly encouraged. The appointment will be subject to the German law on fixed-term contracts in science (WissZeitVG).

jobs.occupation: Global Procurement Specialist / Strategic Buyer (m/f/d) (Fachkaufmann/-frau - Einkauf und Logistik)
jobs.description:
About us European Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (ESMC) GmbH is
the joint venture between TSMC, Bosch, Infineon and NXP. For the first
time, global technology leader TSMC is building a semiconductor fab in
the heart of Europe, offering cutting-edge manufacturing technologies
for next-generation semiconductor products. ESMC represents a shared
commitment to strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. For
our future fab in Dresden, we are looking for a highly motivated and
committed: Global Procurement Specialist / Strategic Buyer (m/f/d) Are
you ready to secure the supply chain for Europe’s pioneer
semiconductor Greenfield project? As a Global Procurement Specialist /
Strategic Buyer, you will take ownership of the commercial end-to-end
sourcing process for critical materials supporting our brand-new
manufacturing site in Dresden. You will negotiate high-volume global
contracts, mitigate supply chain risks, and build resilient
partnerships with key international suppliers. If you thrive at the
intersection of business strategy, cross-functional collaboration, and
high-tech operations, this role offers you the ultimate platform to
make a global impact. Tasks Strategic Sourcing: Develop, negotiate,
and execute end-to-end global sourcing strategies and contracts to
ensure a highly resilient, cost-effective supply of critical
materials. Supplier Partnership Management: Build and nurture
long-term strategic relationships with a global supplier base to
secure high-quality materials and services. Commercial Negotiation:
Lead commercial negotiations, drive total cost of ownership (TCO)
optimization, and actively manage commercial risks. Performance
Monitoring : Evaluate and manage supplier performance against key
quality, delivery, cost, and risk metrics to ensure full contract
compliance. Risk & Supply Resilience: Proactively identify and resolve
supplier-related issues, including delivery disruptions and quality
deviations, using data-driven preventive actions. Cross-Functional
Alignment: Collaborate closely with engineering, fab operations,
finance, and HQ procurement teams to align sourcing activities with
production budgets and timelines. Process Excellence: Contribute to
continuous improvement initiatives to streamline procurement workflows
and scale up supply chain operations. Governance & ESG: Ensure strict
compliance with all internal policies, contractual obligations, trade
laws, and ESG standards across all purchasing activities. Profile
Required: Education: Bachelor’s degree or higher in Supply Chain
Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, IT, or a
related field. Experience: Minimum of 4 years of strategic procurement
or supply chain experience within an international industrial setting.
Negotiation Skills: Proven track record in commercial negotiations,
contract management, and strategic supplier evaluation. Languages:
Proficiency in English (C1) and German (C1) is required for seamless
collaboration with local and global stakeholders. Mindset: Strong
analytical thinking, attention to detail in contract review, and the
ability to coordinate multiple complex projects simultaneously.
International Onboarding: Willingness to complete an intensive
training of 3-6 months at TSMC Taiwan. Nice to have: Industry
Knowledge: Prior experience in the semiconductor, chemical, or
advanced materials industry. Certifications: Professional supply chain
or procurement certifications (e.g., APICS CPIM/CSCP, ISM CPSM).
Global Mindset: Experience in collaborating with Asian business
environments; Mandarin language skills are a plus. Why Join ESMC? Help
build a completely new semiconductor manufacturing site in Europe.
Work in a highly international environment with colleagues across the
world. Shape processes instead of maintaining existing structures.
Participate in global projects and cross-functional collaboration.
Additional contact details Please apply with an English resume.

for on-the-road payment solutions, you will work in an exciting
environment. Our tasks are defined by our Purpose: To drive the

reality? Then join our team! You can look forward to exciting
challenges, an inspiring environment, and a work culture that combines
flexibility and collaboration – with our 60/40 hybrid model and

IT Security, Enterprise Architecture, and Service Management teams.

continuously improving complex IT infrastructures, including their
documentation and modeling. You possess hands-on experience with ITSM
platforms, CMDB solutions, and their integration into enterprise IT
environments. You have practical experience in IT Asset Management and

criticality, risk, and protection requirements. You have a strong
understanding of the interdependencies between IT architecture, CMDB,
asset inventory management, CIAA classification, security

industry standards and frameworks such as ITIL, ISMS, as well as

changing customer needs. That's how we stay mobile and master every
challenge the future holds. There are also many other good reasons to
work at DKV Mobility. For example, we offer you comprehensive company
health management, parent-child offices (from 2023) and support you in

importance to work-life balance. We stand for the compatibility of

jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for a

Research associate (m/f/x) in Data Science in Chemistry

At the Chair of Inorganic Chemistry II of the Ruhr University Bochum we address research questions in the fields of organometallic synthesis chemistry and homogeneous catalysis. We are an internationally oriented research team that develops new reagents as well as highly efficient catalysts for synthetic chemistry. By combining advanced synthetic methods, state of the art analytical techniques, quantum chemical calculations, and machine learning methods, we conduct world leading research at the highest international level. Automated analysis of chemical data and the prediction of reactivity, selectivity and yield by means of machine learning are revolutionising modern chemistry. In our group we employ data science methods together with quantum chemical calculations to model reaction networks from experimental data, understand bonding situations and reactivities, and identify new catalysts and reaction conditions in a data driven way.

The Chair of Inorganic Chemistry II (Organometallic Chemistry and Homogeneous Catalysis) is looking for a full time scientific staff member (postdoctoral researcher) (100 % TV L 13) to start immediately. We are looking for a motivated postdoctoral researcher (m/f/x) who, with a passion for interdisciplinary work, will support the design of teaching courses in data science and machine learning and strengthen our group in this area.

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 2 Jahre
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-09-21

Your tasks:

- Quantum‑chemical calculations – perform calculations to elucidate reaction mechanisms, bonding situations and to extract physicochemical properties of molecules
- Model development & validation – create and validate models that clarify structure‑activity relationships and predict properties and reactivities; analyse data with statistical methods and visualise the results
- Collaboration with experimentalists – work closely with laboratory scientists to support and validate data collection
- Project leadership – take responsibility for projects, supervise students, write reports and grant proposals
- Scientific communication – compile results into publications and assist students in preparing manuscripts
- Mentorship – supervise students in their theses and support teaching activities in the areas of Data Science and Machine Learning
- Teaching – support the development and implementation of new student courses in Data Science and Machine Learning

Your profile:

A candidate with a completed university degree and a PhD (preferred) in Chemistry is sought; candidates from related fields such as Data Science or Computer Science with demonstrable knowledge of chemistry are also welcome.

Further requirements:

- Practical experience in quantum‑chemical calculations – familiarity with common quantum‑chemical programs and methods, in particular ORCA, Multiwfn, AIM, etc.
- Practical experience in machine learning & chemistry‑specific data science – programming skills in Python and hands‑on experience with standard libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, pandas, Scikit‑learn, RDKit, PyTorch, etc.
- Practical experience in homogeneous catalysis – desirable, but not mandatory
- Practical experience with the installation and maintenance of high-performance computing clusters – desirable, but not mandatory
- Theoretical knowledge in quantum-chemistry, machine learning, molecular chemistry
- Experience in research project management
- Experience in publishing and presenting scientific results
- Experience in teaching and the supervision of students and interns
- Language skills – English (fluent spoken and written) is required; German is an advantage but not mandatory

Furthermore, the applicant should be open to team‑oriented work and possess a strong motivation for interdisciplinary research.

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ), Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University (HHU) Düsseldorf is an interdisciplinary research institute that integrates basic, translational and clinical research to improve the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of diabetes mellitus and its complications. The Institute for Clinical Biochemistry and Pathobiochemistry (Director: Prof. Dr. Hadi Al-Hasani) investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying insulin resistance, skeletal muscle metabolism and type 2 diabetes.

For a new research project, we are looking for a talented and highly motivated

Doctoral Student (PhD / Dr. rer. nat., m/f/div., E13 TV-L 65%)

to join our interdisciplinary research team investigating the molecular mechanisms by which repeated
cold exposure improves skeletal muscle insulin sensitivity.

Insulin resistance of skeletal muscle is a key feature in the development of type 2 diabetes, accounting for the majority of impaired postprandial glucose disposal. While lifestyle interventions such as exercise are well established, repeated cold exposure has recently emerged as a promising strategy to improve insulin sensitivity in humans, with reported improvements of up to 40%. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying these beneficial metabolic adaptations remain largely unknown.

The project aims to identify the signaling pathways responsible for cold-induced improvements in skeletal muscle insulin action. A particular focus will be placed on testing the hypothesis that mild cold-induced muscle activation ("micro-shivering"), rather than brown adipose tissue activation, mediates these metabolic benefits.

The project combines translational human studies with mechanistic investigations in mouse models and offers extensive training in state-of-the-art metabolic and molecular research techniques.
Proteomic analysis of human skeletal muscle biopsies obtained from cold acclimation studies to identify molecular signatures associated with improved insulin sensitivity.
Mechanistic studies in wild-type and UCP1-deficient mice to investigate the effects of cold exposure and muscle activation on glucose uptake and insulin action.
Functional characterization of established and novel regulators of skeletal muscle metabolism, including AMPK, GLUT4, Rac1 and newly identified candidate proteins.
Investigation of GLUT4 trafficking and insulin signaling using advanced molecular and cellular approaches.

The project offers training in:

Mass spectrometry-based proteomics
Mouse models of insulin resistance and metabolic disease
Indirect calorimetry and metabolic phenotyping
Glucose uptake assays in isolated skeletal muscle
Molecular biology techniques (Western blotting, qPCR, gene expression analyses)
Immunohistochemistry and skeletal muscle fibre typing

In vivo electroporation and functional gene manipulation
Fluorescence-based analysis of GLUT4 translocation

You hold (or are close to obtaining) a Master's degree in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Molecular Medicine, Physiology, Biomedical Sciences or a related discipline.
You have practical experience in molecular and cellular biology techniques such as Western blotting, qPCR and cell culture.
Experience with metabolic phenotyping, skeletal muscle biology, mouse models or proteomics is advantageous but not required.
You enjoy interdisciplinary research and are interested in combining human physiology with mechanistic laboratory studies.
You are highly motivated, curious, and able to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment.
You have an excellent command of written and spoken English.

PhD student: Plant RNA Biology
The Wachter group at the Institute for Molecular Physiology (Faculty 10: Biology of Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz) investigates the molecular mechanisms and biological functions of alternative RNA splicing in plants. Our recent work identified a structured mRNA element that regulates specific DEAD-box helicase genes and revealed their critical role in controlling alternative splicing. Intriguingly, these functions appear to be linked to unique C-terminal features of the respective helicases. As a member of an interdisciplinary and international research team, you will investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the splicing-regulatory activity of these DEAD-box helicases, with a particular focus on the functional relevance of RGG motifs, subcellular localisation, and their potential involvement in phase separation. In collaboration with the Weinberg group (University Halle-Wittenberg), you will also explore how helicase targeting of pre-mRNA structural elements may intersect with the binding of splicing regulators to determine splice site choice. Your research will employ a multidisciplinary approach that integrates molecular biology, RNA biochemistry, cell biology, and plant physiology, with Arabidopsis thaliana as the primary model system. You will benefit from extensive expertise, various core facilities, and a completely new research infrastructure. The PhD project is funded by the DFG and can be integrated in the international PhD programme (IPP) in Mainz.

The IUF - Leibniz Research Institute for Environmental Medicine investigates the molecular mechanisms by which environmental factors - including particles, radiation, and chemical exposures - affect human health. The institute’s research focuses on environmentally induced aging and disease processes in the pulmonary system and skin, as well as environmentally driven dysfunctions of the nervous and immune systems. By developing innovative, human-relevant experimental model systems, the IUF contributes to improved environmental risk assessment and to the identification of novel strategies for the prevention and treatment of environmentally induced health damage.

The position is part of the DFG-funded research project Adaptive Sampling for Variable Selection and Prediction on Large-Scale Genome-Exposome Data. The project develops scalable statistical learning methods for large biomedical datasets from cohorts such as the UK Biobank and NAKO, integrating genetic and environmental variables to understand and predict health phenotypes. The focus is on adaptive sampling, high-dimensional variable selection, Bayesian uncertainty quantification and interpretable machine learning. The doctoral researcher will develop, implement and apply new statistical methodology.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

At the Chair of Mechanical Process Engineering (www.mvt.ovgu.de), we are a group of enthusiastic researchers with extensive research activities in the numerical modelling of multiphase flows. Our work addresses the fundamental physical mechanisms governing dispersed and interfacial multiphase flows, as well as their application to engineering systems. Current research topics include particle-laden and droplet-laden turbulent flows, particle–turbulence and droplet–turbulence interactions, the dynamics of non-spherical particles, interfacial flows, and compressible and incompressible multiphase-flow applications. Approximately eight PhD researchers and three postdoctoral researchers currently work in this area at the Chair.

The objective of the advertised position is to attract a junior group leader who will take a leading role in our computational multiphase-flow research. The successful candidate will contribute to and help coordinate ongoing research projects, while also establishing their own research direction within the Chair. The position offers excellent opportunities to develop an independent academic profile and to pursue a Habilitation. It therefore combines scientific leadership in existing activities with the opportunity to initiate new research topics and contribute to the further development of our numerical methods and simulation tools.

Our in-house simulation framework includes state-of-the-art methods for immersed boundaries, Lagrangian particle and droplet tracking, non-spherical particle dynamics, particle and droplet interactions, gas–liquid interfaces, large-eddy simulation, and fully coupled solvers for compressible and incompressible flows. You will also have the opportunity to establish your own teaching portfolio in areas such as numerical methods, multiphase flows, or particle technology.

*The position is full time for a period of 3 years with the opportunity to extend by a further 3 years.

Job description:

- Develop, implement, and analyse analytical and numerical models for multiphase flows
- Establish an independent research profile in computational multiphase-flow modelling
- Lead and coordinate the further development of our in-house simulation tools in C and MPI
- Develop research ideas and prepare proposals for externally funded research projects
- Supervise PhD researchers, postdoctoral researchers, and students working in computational multiphase flows
- Contribute to teaching in multiphase flows, numerical methods, particle technology, or related subjects
- Contribute to the scientific development and coordination of the computational multiphase-flow group
- Opportunity for further scientific qualification, including the possibility to pursue a Habilitation

Requirements profile:

- A Master’s degree or equivalent and a PhD in mechanical engineering, process engineering, aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, physics, or a related discipline
- A strong background in the physical and numerical modelling of fluid-mechanical or multiphase-flow problems
- Demonstrated research experience in computational multiphase flows, such as particle-laden, droplet-laden, or interfacial flows
- Strong scientific-programming skills in C, C++, or Fortran, including experience with MPI and high-performance computing
- Experience in developing numerical methods or simulation software; expertise in techniques such as immersed-boundary methods, Lagrangian tracking, interface-capturing methods, or particle-interaction models is desirable
- A strong publication record commensurate with your career stage, together with the ability to develop independent research ideas and contribute to research proposals
- Excellent written and spoken English, as well as a good command of German or a commitment to acquiring sufficient German proficiency for teaching and administrative duties within two years

* Designing scalable, secure Azure and Snowflake architectures by translating complex requirements from the global manufacturing network into future-proof cloud solutions

What You Bring

* Master's degree in Computer Science, Business Informatics, Cloud Engineering, or a related field, paired with many years of experience in cloud architecture

* Strong strategic planning and influencing skills: you're as comfortable shaping a multi-year architecture roadmap as you are aligning stakeholders across a complex, matrixed organization

Our Grid Technology division enables a reliable, sustainable, and digital grid. The power grid is the backbone of the energy transition. Siemens Energy offers a leading portfolio and solutions in HVDC transmission, grid stabilization and storage, high voltage switchgears and transformers, and digital grid technology.  

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical 

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.

For Applicants applying from Austria:

At Siemens Energy we offer competitive compensation and additional benefits based on your performance, experience and qualification. Due to the Austrian legal regulations, we are obliged to state the minimum salary for this position. Please note that there is a clear willingness for a higher compensation considering your individual expectations, expertise and skills. The minimum salary for this position in the collective agreement for the electrical and electronics industry is in the amount of 54.439,39 € gross/year for a full-time position (38,5 h/week).

jobs.occupation: PhD Student in Computational Chemistry (f/m/d) (Pay scale 13 TV-L, 67 %) (Chemiker/in)
jobs.description:
We are a young, innovative university in the middle of the Metropole Ruhr. Excellent in research and teaching, we think in terms of possibilities instead of limits and develop ideas with a future. We live diversity, promote potential and are committed to educational equity.
The University of Duisburg-Essen invites applications for the position of a
PhD Student in Computational Chemistry (f/m/d) (Pay scale 13 TV-L, 67 %) (gross 38.265 – 54.388 €)
at the Faculty of Chemistry, Institute for Physical Chemistry (located at the campus in Essen).
The Faculty of Chemistry at the UDE is one of the largest chemistry faculties in Germany and offers three study programs under one roof: Chemistry, Water Science and Chemistry Teachers College. The young and dynamic research group led by Prof. Dr. Erna K. Wieduwilt focuses on elucidating the structures and reactions of transition-metal enzymes with computer simulations, thereby bridging the fields of computational chemistry and quantum crystallography.

Your tasks

You will conduct research within the project “Boosting Enzymatic Plastic Recycling via Future Computing” as part of the NRW Return Programme of Prof. Dr. Erna K. Wieduwilt. The main focus of your position will be on evaluating quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations on metalloenzymes and exploring whether machine learning can be used for predictions of enzymatic reactions in biomass and plastic degradation. In these areas, you will closely collaborate with postdoctoral and PhD researchers who have experience in QM/MM calculations of metalloenzymes and machine learning. Additionally, you will contribute to supervising students, teaching activities, and administrative tasks, aligned with your transferable skill development.

Your profile

- By the time of appointment, you will have successfully completed your university studies in chemistry, biochemistry, cheminformatics, bioinformatics, biology, physics or a related field with a standard period of study of at least eight semesters (minimum 270 credit points or equivalent) and an average grade of at least ‘good’ (or equivalent)
- You are highly motivated to pursue research in sustainable chemistry and push the boundaries of computational biochemistry
- Ideally, you have first experience in QM calculations and their analysis. Experience with QM/MM or QM-cluster calculations on enzymes is desirable but not required; you are eager to learn these methods
- Previous experience in the use of machine learning and/or QM software packages, high-performance computing (HPC) clusters, and Linux operating systems will be considered an advantage
- You demonstrate scientific curiosity, take responsibility for your own work, and actively contribute to team-oriented, interdisciplinary, and international collaborations inside and outside the research group. Fluency in English (written and spoken) is essential
The position offers the opportunity for further scientific qualification.

We offer

- An interesting and responsible research position with broad opportunities for academic and personal growth, allowing you to take responsibility and establish valuable connections with academic and industrial collaborators locally as well as internationally
- A supportive and appreciative working atmosphere within a highly motivated, international and diverse research group. We look forward to welcoming and onboarding our new team member
- Fully funded participation in national and international workshops, summer schools, and conferences as well as dedicated presentation training
- Training in state-of-the-art computational methods and software (e.g., ORCA, AMBER) as well as access to significant HPC resources (e.g., the cluster AmplitUDE (https://escience-wissr.gitpages.uni-due.de/hpc-support/content/amplitUDE/amplitude_hardware.html) )
- Access to graduate courses, transferable skills training and the possibility to apply for the Water Graduate School (WGS (https://www.uni-due.de/zwu/wgs.php) )
- Family-friendly policies, including childcare support
- Advisory services for employees with family care responsibilities
- Possibility to enrol as a student, granting access to student housing, local public transport throughout Germany (Deutschlandsemesterticket (https://www.uni-due.de/faq-studium/semesterticket_en.php) ) and discounts at university canteens, museums, etc.
- Excellent public transport connections and free parking
- Access to attractive sports and health programs (university sports)
- The possibility of remote work
Starting date: 01.12.2026
Contract period: 36 months (3 years) with the possibility of extension
Working time: 67% of a full-time employment (part-time employment is possible)
Application deadline: 25.09.2026
Please submit your application (motivation letter, CV, diplomas, transcript of records with grades, at least two references) quoting reference 416-26 to: Prof. Dr. Erna K. Wieduwilt, Universität Duisburg-Essen, Fakultät für Chemie, Campus Essen, 45117 Essen. Please compile your application in a single PDF file and send it via email to applications.wieduwilt@uni-due.de.
Additional information about our research and group can be found at:
- About the project “Boosting Enzymatic Plastic Recycling via Future Computing”: https://www.uni-due.de/2025-12-08-professor-erna-wieduwilt-researches-plastic-recycling
- About the group: https://www.linkedin.com/posts/erna-wieduwilt_scienceisteamwork-chemistry-mint-activity-7482096217875857408-1d_R?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desk-top&rcm=ACoAADDOYrUBY5t0a3GvPalmhq6zjRkeWRjRhdk (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/erna-wieduwilt_scienceisteamwork-chemistry-mint-activity-7482096217875857408-1d_R?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desk-top&rcm=ACoAADDOYrUBY5t0a3GvPalmhq6zjRkeWRjRhdk)
- Current webpage: https://www.uni-due.de/zmb/members/erna-wieduwilt.php
The University of Duisburg-Essen is committed to promoting diversity among its members (see https://www.uni-due.de/diversity/en/). It aims to increase the number of women in academic positions and therefore explicitly encourages qualified women to apply. Women will be given preference in accordance with the North Rhine-Westphalia State Equality Act (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz NRW) if they have equivalent qualifications. Applications from suitable severely disabled persons and persons of equal status within the meaning of Section 2 (3) SGB IX are welcome.

At Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.
The Position
Join our dynamic team at Boehringer Ingelheim as a Customer Experience (CX) Head, TA. In this pivotal role, you will be the strategic linchpin, leveraging data to enrich decision-making and uncovering new business opportunities within the TA. Working in close collaboration with the TA Head and a standing member of the Brand Team, you will drive customer-centric initiatives for Human Pharma Germany. If you're passionate about shaping customer experiences and have a knack for strategic thinking, we'd love to hear from you.

- Integral analytical support for OL, ACV and LTF planning process and preparations on a strategic level

- Establishing strategic and cooperative relationships with various functions within HP Business Operations and cross-functional teams will be a major part of your role.
- You will serve as a liaison between various functions and groups (Brand Team, HP Operations Group Heads and Squad Leads), influencing stakeholders to improve productivity, manage necessary changes, and support key business projects.

Join our Compression Regional Service Sales within Siemens Energy TI Compression as a Client Manager supporting customers from the Oil & Gas, chemical and industrial sectors.

The Client Manager is the owner of the client relationship, and is responsible for ensuring customer satisfaction, meeting client requirements and driving Services bookings growth within their respective territory. He/she leads all aspects of business and opportunity development from the initial stages through order entry. 

This position is primarily focused on Germany (Western & Eastern part) market and reports to the Head of Sales REGION WE, SWE, NORDICS and GERMANY.

You will be involved in some of the most exciting and challenging service and modernization projects within these industries. This is a highly networked role that requires an ability to work under challenging deadlines. 

 

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Develop and manage long-term relationships with assigned clients
* Proactively and systematically prospect the market aiming to generate new leads and opportunities.
* Understand the evaluation and decision-making process of customers and develop a strategy to position Siemens Energy ahead of the competition. 
* Develop and execute the sales capture plan (annual plan) and strategy around each customer in your responsibilities, incorporating the customer needs, equipment application, Siemens Energy strengths, competitor’s weaknesses and a robust market level pricing recommendation based on the assessment of competitive position.
* Identify advanced business opportunities (LMU) and support RPDM in developing and successfully closing such opportunities.
* Identify, create and maintain a robust opportunity pipeline in Salesforce to support overall business sales target. Own the Sales target in the assigned territory. Effectively manage opportunities via CRM Tool (Salesforce.com), ensuring opportunities are regularly updated
* Maintain the accuracy (within SFDC) of the entire installed equipment population, including operating status and planned outages, and client data in the assigned territory
* Prepare, coordinate and conduct proposal negotiations until closure of the opportunities in cooperation with other involved professionals
* Conduct Win/Loss analyses and provide input to fighting guides and regional competitive analyses.
* Provide voice of the client needs/competitive intelligence, market drivers and buying influences for the development of new product and service offerings

What You Bring

* Proven track record in driving results, delivering on growth strategies and proactive creation & conversion of sales opportunities in complex market environments
* Bachelor of Science in Engineering required with a minimum 5 years of experience in Energy industry and at least 3 years in sales/business development role.
* Turbomachinery experience/knowledge is mandatory, strong technical understanding of industrial compressors is preferred.

jobs.occupation: Research Group Leader for the Research Area C: Power – Violence – Trauma (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description:
Tasks

The University of Bonn is an international research university offering a broad range of subjects. With a 200-year history, some 31,500 students, more than 6,000 employees and an outstanding reputation in Germany and abroad, the University of Bonn is one of the leading universities in Germany and has been awarded the status of a University of Excellence.

The Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS) is looking to fill the following position with effect from 1 January 2027, on a fixed-term contract until 31 December 2032:

Research Group Leader for the Research Area C: Power – Violence – Trauma

The BCDSS, a German Research Council-funded “Cluster of Excellence”, offers excellent opportunities for inter-disciplinary and comparative research of different forms of Strong Asymmetrical Dependencies (SADs) across time periods and world regions. During its first phase (2019–2025), the BCDSS successfully developed the con-cept of SAD as a comprehensive analytical framework to understand how power imbalances have been shaped in the past, and continue to influence, societies around the world today. In its second funding phase (2026–2032), the BCDSS will investigate the underlying causes and mechanisms that contribute to the persistence of SADs across historical and contemporary contexts. We aim to anchor Historically Informed Dependency Studies (HIDS) as a key interdisciplinary field in the humanities, encouraging scholars across the humanities and social sciences to systematically integrate the analysis of SADs into the study of social, economic, and cultural phe-nomena.

Our research focuses on five Research Areas:

- Transitions and Transformations of SADs,
- Economies of SADs,
- Power – Violence – Trauma,
- Cultural Heritage – Transitional Justice – Memory Cultures,
- Alternative Archives and Life Writing.

The successful candidate will lead a Research Group in the BCDSS' Research Area C “Power – Violence – Trau-ma”, design and conduct independent projects in the field of Historically Informed Dependency Studies (HIDS) that closely relate to the Research Area's research goals. Topics can be of a wide variety – from micro studies to wide scale approaches, in any historical period or geographical region. A Research Group at the BCDSS is an independent research unit led by an early-career researcher to pursue an original research agenda while su-pervising a small team of researchers. The successful candidate will recruit two doctoral researchers for the research group and collaborate closely with colleagues from the BCDSS, in particular the cluster professor for Trauma Studies/ History of Violence. Furthermore, the successful candidate will be part of the interdisciplinary and international research community. 

Your tasks:

- Developing the research profile of the Research Group on the historical relation-ship between violence, trauma, and coercion within the field of Historically In-formed Dependency Studies (HIDS),
- Recruiting and supervising two doctoral researchers,
- Providing academic leadership and strategic development of the Research Group and Research Area C,
- Conducting an independent research project leading to a second monograph or equivalent work,
- Developing innovative theoretical and methodological approaches to analyse SAD,
- Organizing and contributing to international workshops, seminars, and confer-ences,
- Building national and international research networks.

Your profile

- At least three years of postdoctoral experience and an excellent academic track record in one or more of the following fields: the history of violence, trauma studies, historical psychology (excluding the history of psychoanalysis), or a related discipline represented at the BCDSS (e.g. Anthropology, Archaeology, Art History, History, Law, Regional Studies, Sociology, or Theology),
- Publications relevant to the BCDSS research agenda in general and Research Area C in particular,
- Native or near-native proficiency in English,
- A strong interest in advancing research on HIDS from a comparative and interdisciplinary perspective,
- Demonstrated ability to develop innovative research questions and engage with methodological and epistemological challenges,
- Experience in collaborative and interdisciplinary research.

Wir bieten

- The opportunity to establish and lead an independent Research Group, including the recruitment and supervision of two doctoral researchers,
- Membership in the interdisciplinary and international research environment of the Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS),
- An open, collaborative, and innovative research culture that encourages interdis-ciplinary exchange,
- Mentoring by two senior professors and comprehensive opportunities for profes-sional and leadership development,
- Excellent institutional support for independent research, career development, families, and equal opportunities,
- Many options available for university sports,
- Excellent access by public transport thanks to Bonn's central location as well as the opportunity to take advantage of low-cost parking,
- Flexible working hours and the ability to work from home,
- Remuneration in accordance with TV-L pay grade 14.

Your application needs to include:

- Cover letter stating your motivation to work at the BCDSS (max. 1800 characters including spaces),
- Curriculum Vitae,
- A copy of your PhD certificate,
- An outline of the proposed Research Group (max. 10.000 characters including spaces). Please include information on:
- Key research questions and hypotheses;
- originality of the proposed project vis-à-vis existing scholarship and key publications in the field (with bibliography),
- alignment of the project with the BCDSS' research goals in general,
- relevance of the project to Research Area C in particular and, if applicable, cross-connections to other Research Areas,
- concise ideas for two PhD projects,
- The name and contact of two referees (position, professional address, and e-mail).

The University of Bonn promotes an open, respectful, and non-discriminatory academic culture and is actively committed to equal opportunity and family friendliness. We aim to eliminate structural disadvantages and to strengthen diversity in research, teaching, and administration. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regardless of ethnic or social background, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability, or age.

Applications from women and people with a documented severe disability (or equivalent status) will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equality Act (LGG) NRW and Social Code (SGB) IX.

If you are interested in this position, please send your complete application to application@dependency.uni-bonn.de by September 15, 2026, quoting reference 2026/387. For technical reasons, applications may only be submitted by email as a single PDF file. Please do not hesitate to contact BCDSS Managing Director Jeannine Bischoff (dependency@uni-bonn.de) if you need any more information.

The Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, with its tradition spanning more than 600 years, is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With over 1,300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and serves as a training center for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Epidemiologist to design and conduct epidemiological research in pediatric populations, focusing on the determinants of child health, the development of common childhood diseases, particularly obesity, and the prevention and long-term outcomes of childhood obesity and metabolic diseases.
The research group "Childhood Obesity and Metabolic Research", led by Antje Körner, investigates the development, mechanisms and health consequences of childhood obesity. The translational approach combines experimental research, clinical studies and genetic approaches. Our international and interdisciplinary team is closely integrated with the research structures of the Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, Helmholtz Munich, and leading local as well as national research consortia, such as the Excellence cluster LeiCeM, the German Center for Child and Youth Health (DZKJ), and our large children's and adolescents' cohort LIFE Child.
We have large, well-characterized cohorts up and running with a longitudinal setting and across the entire age range: LIFE Child (n~6000), Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort (n~2500), and Leipzig Adipose Tissue Childhood cohort (n~700), with deep phenotyping allowing for combining clinical, epidemiological, lifestyle and functional omics and multi-omics data.
Key Responsibilities

- Design, plan, and conduct epidemiological research projects, including cohort and intervention studies.
- Develop study protocols and statistical analysis plans.
- Analyze and interpret complex population-based, clinical, and/or health-related datasets.
- Preparation of scientific manuscripts, reports, presentations, and grant applications.
- Ensure high standards of data quality, reproducibility, and compliance with ethical and data protection regulations.
- Present research findings at national and international conferences and scientific meetings.
- Provide methodological expertise and consultation to ongoing research projects; collaborate closely with clinicians, statisticians, bioinformaticians, and other researchers
- Supervision junior researchers or students.

Required Qualifications
Education: Candidates should have a Ph.D. and/or M.D. degree in: Epidemiology, Public Health, Biostatistics, Medicine, Health Sciences or a related discipline.
Professional Experience

- Experience in the design and implementation of epidemiological studies, large cohort studies.
- Experience working with large-scale health, clinical, or population-based datasets.
- Strong understanding of epidemiological study designs and methodologies.
- Experience with observational and interventional research.
- Experience in data cleaning, validation, and quality assurance.
- Familiarity with evidence-based medicine and public health principles.
- Track record of scientific publications in peer-reviewed journals is desirable.
- Experience in interdisciplinary and collaborative research environments.
- Knowledge of research ethics and data protection requirements.
- Experience in grant writing is an advantage.
- Knowledge of causal inference methods (e.g., Target Trial Emulation, Mendelian Randomization) is desirable.

Statistical and Analytical Skills

- Proficiency in at least one statistical programming language such as: R, SAS, Stata, Python.
- Experience with general statistical methods:
- Regression modeling
- Longitudinal data analysis
- Missing data methods
- Sensitivity analyses
- Knowledge of modern analytical approaches, including machine learning methods, is an advantage.

Personal Competencies

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
- Excellent organizational and project management abilities.
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.
- Communication skills: English - excellent; German - very good

Candidates with one or more of the following areas of expertise are particularly encouraged to apply:

- Cohort studies
- Precision medicine and risk prediction modeling
- Multi-omics, biomarker, or biobank data integration
- Obesity, diabetes, cardiovascular disease, or metabolic health research

At the Faculty of Computer Science, Institute of Computer Engineering, the Chair of Compiler Construction offers a full-time project position in the context of the Skywalker Project (Skyrmionics-aware and Compiler-centric Racetrack Architecture) as

Research Associate (m/f/x)

(subject to personal qualification employees are remunerated according to salary group E 13 TV-L)

starting as soon as possible. The position is funded by DFG and is limited to three years, with the possibility of extension, subject to further availability of funding. The period of employment is governed by § 2 (2) Fixed Term Research Contracts Act (Wissenschaftszeitvertragsgesetz – WissZeitVG).

Tasks:

At the Chair of Compiler Construction, we pursue a long-term vision of shaping how future electronic systems are programmed. Our research includes definition of novel programming methods and compiler infrastructures for future computing systems across both the embedded and high-performance computing domains. Within the Skywalker project, we specifically focus on skyrmionics-racetrack memories (SK-RTMs), targeting cross-layer design and optimization opportunities. This is a joint project with Prof. Jian-Jia Chen from RWTH Aachen, alongside partner institutions from leading Taiwanese universities with extensive expertise in chip design and racetrack memory research. The successful candidate will focus on exploring and developing novel analysis and optimization techniques to fully exploit the potential of SK-RTM technologies across different system configurations, while simultaneously mitigating the impact of associated challenges — including sequentiality constraints and reliability concerns.

Requirements: 

We aim to attract the best talent in the respective research fields and expect the following:

- an outstanding university and, if applicable, PhD degree (or equivalent) in computer science, mathematics, electrical engineering, or a relevant area
- research experience, preferably in programming languages, compilers, applied mathematics, and optimization techniques
- a strong background in compiler, code generation, computer architecture and RTM physics would be beneficial
- an independent, target- and solution-driven work attitude
- inter- and multidisciplinary thinking
- an integrative and cooperative personality with excellent communication and social skills
- fluency in English (written and oral)
- knowledge of compiler frameworks such as LLVM IR, TVM, or MLIR is highly beneficial

We offer:

You will join a team of enthusiastic scientists who creatively pursue their individual research agenda inspired by the Skywalker goals in particular and the overall chair’s mission in general. The candidate will also benefit from the vibrant research community around machine learning of the SCADS.AI center (https://scads.ai (https://scads.ai/) ), the active-3D cluster (https://active3d-trr404.de (https://active3d-trr404.de/) ), the recently granted COMETH project (supported by the prestigious ERC consolidator grant) and the Excellence Cluster REC² (Responsible Electronics in the Climate Change Era).

TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The University is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment.

Application:

Please submit your detailed application (in English only) with a motivation letter, CV, copy of degree certificate, transcript of grades (i.e. the official list of coursework including your grades), and proof of English language skills by September 30, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de/) by sending it as a single pdf file to jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:jeronimo.castrillon@tu-dresden.de) or to:

**TU Dresden, Chair of Compiler Construction, Prof. Jeronimo Castrillon, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.** 

Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.

TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.

Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .

Your role: Laboratory Assistant in Quality Control (m/f/d)

The position is initially limited to 2 years.

In this technically demanding role, you will be largely responsible for the practical implementation and maintenance of our analytical test procedures. Your focus will be on ensuring robust analysis in accordance with international standards directly in the laboratory.

Your Responsibilities:

- Wide-ranging analysis: You will apply chromatographic (HPLC, GC) and wet chemical methods to ensure precise quality control, maintaining data integrity through GMP-compliant documentation and modern laboratory standards (e.g., 5S).
- Pharmacopoeia compliance: You will independently establish and verify analytical methods according to applicable monographs (e.g. EP, USP) and carry out verifications in regulatory revisions.
- Method optimization & CAPA management: You will experimentally investigate and optimize analytical procedures in the context of deviations and CAPA measures to sustainably increase methodological robustness.
- Conducting validation studies: You will carry out method validations and verifications for new products and feedstocks practically on the device and strictly comply with GMP requirements.
- Securing method transfer (APVs): You will develop "best practices" for analytics and record them in supplementary audit regulations (APVs) to ensure consistent application of the methods across the team.

What You Need to Succeed (minimum qualifications):

- Education: You have completed training as a chemical laboratory assistant (m/f/d), CTA (m/f/d) or a comparable qualification and 2+ years relevant professional experience in pharmaceutical quality control.
- Expertise: You have in-depth, field-tested knowledge in instrumental analysis (HPLC, GC, spectroscopy) as well as in the application of international pharmacopoeia (EP, USP).
- Languages: Fluent German and good English skills for working with international pharmacopoeia.

What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications)

- Methodological competence: Experience in the practical processing of methodological issues in the context of CAPA processes and in the implementation of method validations.
- Way of working: High level of technical understanding of laboratory processes, work reliably in the implementation of complex monographs and passion for working directly in the laboratory.
- IT affinity: Experience with MS Office and chromatography data systems (e.g. Empower) and SAP.

- Convenient commute: Subsidy for the job ticket and free parking.
- Benefits: Employee share purchase program and corporate benefits platform.

- Location: Kiel, Germany - On-site Work Environment
- Travel: 0%
- Position: Limited contract of 2 years.

TUD Dresden University of Technology, as a University of Excellence, is one of the leading and most dynamic research institutions in Germany. 

The new **Center for Synergy of Systems (SynoSys)** develops transdisciplinary approaches and methods in the fields of network science, data science and citizen science in order to conduct integrative research into complex phenomena at the interfaces between biomedicine, social sciences and life sciences. SynoSys will contribute to the emergence of a scientific vision for healthy human development in which physical and mental health are collectively considered in an increasingly digital and networked social and physical environment. As part of SynoSys the Research Group Computational Social Science is focused on the societal impact of digitalization. The group aims to better understand the dynamics of the complex dissemination of information online and its impact on culture, political behavior and democracy. We employ a broad set of methods, spanning agent-based modeling, time-series analysis, network science and natural language processing, to behavioral experiments in the lab and in the field. Data sources are diverse, either collected from online platforms, recruited participants or data donation approaches. To cover this spectrum, we aim for an inherent transdisciplinary approach and methodological innovation. 

For TUD diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.

Research Associate / PhD Student / PostDoc (m/f/x)

jobs.description:
A Snapshot of Your Day 

Join a dynamic engineering product development team focused on industrial gas turbines for power generation! Each day, you will engage in both independent and collaborative work, tackling various engine component design projects, improvements, and technical challenges. Your role will involve leveraging cutting-edge design and analysis tools while collaborating with global resources to enhance technology. You will continuously learn through hands-on tasks, innovative thinking, and specialized courses, all while sharing ideas and results with colleagues and presenting to internal customers and stakeholders.

How You’ll Make an Impact 

* Contribute to the design of turbine hot gas path components, delivering critical thermal analyses and designs that achieve top-tier performance in efficiency, component life, robustness, and manufacturability
* Enhance the tools landscape by improving classical heat transfer tools, tool chains, and automated workflows, identifying opportunities for AI/ML integration and providing follow-on support
* Advance Conjugate Heat Transfer (CHT) 3D thermal design methodologies for new engines and upgrades, exploring new implementation approaches and methodologies
* Play a vital role in engine and component testing, validating designs and analyses by preparing test predictions and conducting post-test data reduction and analyses

What You Bring

* University degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Materials Engineering, or a related field with a focus on thermo-fluid sciences
* Several years of industrial experience in turbomachinery, thermal design of turbine hot gas path components, fluid systems, or comparable applications
* Strong understanding of heat transfer principles and conjugate heat transfer (CHT)
* More than five years of hands-on experience with FEA, CFD, and CAD tools
* Proficiency in computational methods and programming languages such as APDL and Python
* Excellent communication skills, business-fluent English & German

About the Team

Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet. 

Who is Siemens Energy? 

At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.

Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      

Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideo

Our Commitment to Diversity 

Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. 

Rewards/Benefits 

* In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme
* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder
* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity
* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programs and learning materials are available for this purpose
* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical

We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.
